## **7\. Patient Profile Management** {#7.-patient-profile-management}

### **7.1 UC-35: Search Patient** {#7.1-uc-35:-search-patient}

| Primary Actors | Receptionist | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Receptionist, I want to search for a patient by citizen ID (first), passport, patient code, phone, name or health insurance card number, so that a returning patient is reused instead of getting a duplicate profile. First-time and returning patients follow the same process; the only difference is whether a new profile is created (BR-12). The Doctor can use the same search (Permission Matrix 4.4).  |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Receptionist is signed in (UC-01). 2\. The patient (or guardian) is at the reception counter, or is a priority patient brought directly to the Receptionist (BR-14).  |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Receptionist opens Patient Management (or the search box on the Receptionist Dashboard). 2\. The system shows the search form: Search type (Citizen ID selected by default; Passport, Patient code, Phone, Name, Insurance card number) and Keyword. 3\. The Receptionist selects the search type, enters the keyword and clicks Search. 4\. The system validates the keyword by type: Citizen ID 12 digits; Passport 1 to 15 letters or digits; Phone 10 digits; Name 2 to 100 characters; Insurance card number 15 letters or digits; Patient code not empty. The server repeats the check. 5\. The system searches the patient profiles. Citizen ID, passport, patient code, phone and insurance card number must match exactly (passport, patient code and card number ignore case); the insurance card number is searched among the cards used in previous visits. Name search matches part of the name and ignores case and Vietnamese accents. 6\. The system shows at most 50 results: patient code, full name, date of birth, gender, citizen ID or passport, phone, last visit date, active visit (status, registration code, room). 7\. The Receptionist selects the patient. 8\. The system opens View Patient Information (UC-36).  |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 3): Scan the citizen ID card** 1\. The Receptionist scans the QR code of the CCCD (HW-03); the system fills in the citizen ID. \=\> Continue at step 4\. **AF-02 (at step 3): The patient has no citizen ID (e.g. a child or a foreigner) or does not bring it** 1\. The Receptionist selects another search type (Passport, Phone, Name, Patient code or Insurance card number) and enters the keyword. \=\> Continue at step 4\. **AF-03 (at step 6): Several patients match (e.g. same name)** 1\. The system lists all of them; the Receptionist confirms with the date of birth, phone or guardian. \=\> Continue at step 7\. **AF-04 (at step 6): Exactly one patient matches by citizen ID, passport or patient code** 1\. The system opens UC-36 directly (each identification number belongs to exactly one profile – BR-12). \=\> The use case ends. **AF-05 (at step 6): More than 50 patients match** 1\. The system shows the first 50 patients and MSG68 asking the Receptionist to enter a more specific keyword. \=\> Return to step 3\.  |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 4): Empty keyword or wrong format** 1\. The system shows MSG02 or MSG05 under Keyword and does not search. \=\> Return to step 3\. **EF-02 (at step 6): No patient matches** 1\. The system shows MSG01 and the button Create New Patient Profile, which opens UC-37 with the keyword pre-filled (citizen ID, passport, phone or full name). \=\> The use case ends. **EF-03 (at step 1): The user is not allowed to search patients** 1\. The system shows MSG13. \=\> The use case ends. **EF-04 (at step 5): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. \=\> The use case ends.  |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient is identified, or the Receptionist continues with UC-37. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-12, BR-14, BR-17; Permission Matrix 4.4 (Patient profile – Search); US-06 (Search); Performance (Patient search)  |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG02, MSG05, MSG12, MSG13, MSG68 (new), MSG99  |  |  |

### **7.2 UC-36: View Patient Information** {#7.2-uc-36:-view-patient-information}

| Primary Actors | Receptionist | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Receptionist, I want to view a patient's administrative information and visit history, so that I can confirm the patient's identity, update the profile and register a new visit. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Receptionist is signed in and has found the patient (UC-35) or has just created the profile (UC-37). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Receptionist selects the patient. 2\. The system shows the administrative information: patient code, full name, date of birth (age), gender, citizen ID or passport, phone, address, occupation, ethnicity, nationality, guardian (name, phone, relationship), last insurance card used. Drug allergies are shown read-only as a red label (they are recorded by the Doctor – BR-23). 3\. The system shows the visit history, newest first: registration code, date, room, doctor, visit type, status. Clinical details (findings, results, diagnosis, prescription) are not shown. 4\. The system shows the actions: Update Patient Information (UC-38), Register Examination (UC-40). 5\. The Receptionist selects an action. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 3): No previous visit** 1\. The system shows "No visit history". *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* **AF-02 (at step 3): The patient has an active visit (not Completed, Cancelled or Abandoned)** 1\. The system highlights it with its status, room and exam-fee receipt status, disables Register Examination (BR-17) and shows the action Reprint Ticket (UC-41). *\=\>Continue at step 5\.* **AF-03 (at step 3): The patient has a follow-up appointment today** 1\. The system shows the appointment (date, doctor, previous diagnosis) so that the Receptionist registers the follow-up visit. *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): The patient does not exist** 1\. The system shows MSG41. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 2): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient information is shown. No data is changed; the view is recorded in the audit log (BR-42). Clinical details are only shown to the Doctor (UC-52). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-12, BR-17, BR-23, BR-42; Permission Matrix 4.4 (Patient profile – View) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG41, MSG99 |  |  |

### **7.3 UC-37: Create New Patient Profile** {#7.3-uc-37:-create-new-patient-profile}

| Primary Actors | Receptionist | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Receptionist, I want to create a profile for a first-time patient, so that all their visits are linked to one record. Each personal identification number/citizen ID (passport for foreigners) maps to exactly one profile, so the system blocks duplicates by these numbers (BR-12). A profile can be created without an identification number and completed later (UC-38); duplicate profiles are merged by Admin (UC-87). The Receptionist only enters administrative information; medical history and allergies are recorded by the Doctor (BR-23). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Receptionist is signed in. 2\. Search Patient (UC-35) found no profile for the patient. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Receptionist clicks Create New Patient Profile. 2\. The system shows the form, pre-filled with the search keyword: – Personal: Full name\*, Date of birth\*, Gender\* (Male, Female, Undetermined), Citizen ID or Passport (for foreigners; may be left empty and completed later – BR-12), Phone (required from 18 years old), Address\* with Province/City and Ward/Commune, Occupation, Ethnicity (default Kinh), Nationality (default Viet Nam). Occupation, Ethnicity, Nationality, Province/City and Ward/Commune are selected from the Ministry of Health shared catalogs (BR-46); – Guardian (required under 18 years old): Name\*, Relationship\*, Phone, Address. 3\. The Receptionist enters the data from the patient's documents and clicks Save. 4\. The system checks the required fields, which depend on the age calculated from the date of birth. 5\. The system checks the formats: Citizen ID 12 digits, passport at most 15 characters, phone 10 digits, date of birth not in the future and not more than 120 years ago, full name at most 100 characters. Catalog fields must hold an active value of the shared catalog (BR-46). 6\. The system checks that no profile has the same citizen ID or passport (BR-12). 7\. The system checks for possible duplicates: same full name and date of birth. 8\. The system creates the profile with a unique patient code and records the creation in the audit log. 9\. The system shows MSG04 and opens View Patient Information (UC-36), from which the Receptionist continues with Register Examination (UC-40). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 3): Scan the CCCD** 1\. The system fills in full name, date of birth, gender, citizen ID and address from the QR code (HW-03). *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **AF-02 (at step 7): Possible duplicate found** 1\. The system shows MSG57 with the matching profiles. 2\. If the Receptionist selects one of them, no profile is created \=\>continue in UC-36. 3\. If the Receptionist selects Create anyway \=\>continue at step 8\. **AF-03 (at step 3): The Receptionist clicks Cancel** 1\. The system shows MSG40; after confirmation no profile is created. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at steps 4–5): Required field empty or wrong format** 1\. The system shows MSG02, MSG05 or MSG08 under each wrong field. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 6): The citizen ID or passport already exists** 1\. The system shows MSG19 with the button Open profile, which opens UC-36 of the existing patient. No profile is created. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-03 (at step 8): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; no profile is created. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: a new profile exists with a unique patient code (and a unique citizen ID or passport if provided). A profile without an identification number can be completed later in UC-38; the identification number or passport is required before an electronic prescription is issued. Failure / Cancelled: no profile is created. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-12, BR-23, BR-46; Data rule: Unique identification codes (I.3.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG04, MSG05, MSG08, MSG12, MSG19, MSG40, MSG57, MSG99 |  |  |

### **7.4 UC-38: Update Patient Information** {#7.4-uc-38:-update-patient-information}

| Primary Actors | Receptionist | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Receptionist, I want to update a patient's administrative information when it changes (phone, address, guardian, …), so that the profile stays correct for later visits. The Receptionist cannot change medical history or allergies (BR-23). The Receptionist can also add a missing identification number or passport (BR-12). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Receptionist is signed in and is viewing the patient in UC-36. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Receptionist clicks Update Patient Information. 2\. The system shows the form of UC-37 with the current data; the patient code is read-only and medical history and allergies are not shown in the form (BR-23). 3\. The Receptionist changes the data and clicks Save. 4\. The system checks the required fields and formats (as in UC-37, steps 4–5). 5\. If the citizen ID or passport was added or changed, the system checks that it is not used by another patient (BR-12). 6\. The system saves the changes and records them in the audit log (changed fields with old and new values, Receptionist, time). 7\. The system shows MSG03 and reloads UC-36. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 3): The Receptionist clicks Cancel** 1\. If something was changed, the system shows MSG40; after confirmation nothing is saved. *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-02 (at step 3): The Admin clicks “Lưu thay đổi” without changing any value** 1\. The system returns to UC-36 without saving. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 4): Required field empty or wrong format** 1\. The system shows MSG02, MSG05 or MSG08. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 5): The citizen ID or passport belongs to another patient** 1\. The system shows MSG19 with the button Open profile; nothing is saved. Duplicate profiles are merged by Admin (UC-87). *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-03 (at step 6): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the profile holds the new administrative data. Visits already created keep the insurance data recorded at registration. Failure / Cancelled: nothing is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-12, BR-23, BR-46; Security: Audit trail (IV.2.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG03, MSG05, MSG08, MSG12, MSG19, MSG40, MSG99 |  |  |

### **7.5 UC-39: Update Medical History and Allergies** {#7.5-uc-39:-update-medical-history-and-allergies}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to update the patient's medical history and drug allergies during the examination, so that they are kept in the patient profile and warned about in later prescriptions and visits. Drug allergy is a separate field of the patient profile and is only updated by the Doctor during the examination (BR-23). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Doctor is signed in and is examining the patient: the visit is In Examination (or being concluded) in the Doctor's room and its record is not closed (UC-47). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. On the Current Visit Record screen, the Doctor opens the Medical History & Allergies panel. 2\. The system shows the current data of the patient profile: Medical history (chronic diseases, past surgeries, family history), Drug allergies (list of drug / drug group, reaction, severity), last updated (time, by). 3\. The Doctor adds, changes or removes entries and clicks Save. 4\. The system checks the lengths (each entry at most 255 characters; medical history at most 2,000 characters) and that each allergy has a drug or drug group. 5\. The system saves the data in the patient profile, links the change to the current visit and records it in the audit log (old and new values, Doctor, time). 6\. The system shows MSG03 and shows the allergies as a red label on the examination and prescription screens. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The patient reports no allergy** 1\. The Doctor ticks "No known drug allergy"; the system saves this statement with the time and Doctor. *\=\>Continue at step 5\.* **AF-02 (at step 3): The Doctor clicks Cancel** 1\. If something was changed, the system shows MSG40; after confirmation nothing is saved. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 4): Text too long or allergy without a drug** 1\. The system shows MSG08 or MSG02. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 1): The visit is not in the Doctor's room or the record is closed** 1\. The panel is read-only and the system shows MSG13. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-03 (at step 5): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the patient's medical history and allergies are updated and shown at later steps of the visit (prescription) and in later visits. Failure / Cancelled: nothing is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-19, BR-23, BR-32; Security: Audit trail (IV.2.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG03, MSG08, MSG12, MSG13, MSG40, MSG99 |  |  |

## **8\. Patient Reception** {#8.-patient-reception}

### **8.1 UC-40: Register Examination** {#8.1-uc-40:-register-examination}

| Primary Actors | Receptionist | Secondary Actors | Simulated health insurance portal (through UC-74) |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Receptionist, I want to register a new visit for a patient (priority, visit type, reason and symptoms, examination room), so that the patient is routed to the right room. The system issues a queue number and creates the examination fee receipt. Includes UC-41 and UC-42; extended by UC-74. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Receptionist is signed in. The patient has a profile and the Receptionist is viewing it (UC-36). At least one Active examination room has an assigned doctor. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Receptionist clicks “Đăng ký khám”. The system checks that the patient has no active visit (BR-17). The system opens the registration screen showing the patient’s full name, patient code, date of birth, gender and identification number. The reception type shows “Khám bệnh”. If the patient belongs to a priority group, the Receptionist ticks “Ưu tiên” and selects the “Lý do ưu tiên” (BR-14). The Receptionist selects the “Loại lượt khám”: “BHYT” or “Dịch vụ” (BR-11). For “BHYT”, the Receptionist enters the “Số thẻ BHYT” and clicks “Xác minh”; the system verifies the card (UC-74) and shows the card validity and coverage rate (MSG16). The Receptionist enters the “Lý do khám”\* and selects the “Nơi giới thiệu” (“Tự đến” by default). The system shows the active examination rooms with their department, location and the number of waiting and in-progress patients (UC-42). The Receptionist selects the “Phòng khám”. The Receptionist clicks “Tiếp tục”. The system shows the confirmation screen with the patient information, visit type, reception type, examination room and examination fee (BR-27). The Receptionist checks the summary with the patient and clicks “Xác nhận đăng ký”. The system creates the visit with a unique registration code, the room, the registration time, the next queue number of the room for the day (BR-18), the visit type, priority information, insurance card information (if any), the reception type and the reason for visit. A self-paid visit is Waiting for Payment; an insurance visit is Waiting and joins the examination waiting list immediately (BR-15). The system creates the examination fee receipt with status Pending (BR-09, BR-15, BR-27). The system records the registration in the audit log and shows MSG21. The system prints the examination ticket (UC-41). The Receptionist hands the ticket to the patient. A self-paid patient pays at the cashier (UC-69); an insurance patient goes directly to the room’s waiting area. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | 1.AF-01 (at step 5): Self-paid visit 1.1. The Receptionist selects “Dịch vụ”; no insurance card is entered. 1.2. The use case continues at step 7\. 2.AF-02 (at step 6): The insurance card is not valid,or the Receptionist chooses Self-paid after verification fails (UC-74)  2.1. The system switches the visit type to “Dịch vụ” and discards the card data; the Receptionist informs the patient (BR-13). 2.2. The use case continues at step 7\.  3.AF-03 (at step 6): The insurance portal does not answer 3.1. UC-74 shows MSG20. The Receptionist retries, or switches to Self-paid (UC-74, EF-04). 3.2. If switched to Self-paid, the use case continues as in AF-02. 4.AF-04 (at step 3): The patient has a follow-up appointment within its validity period 4.1. The system shows a follow-up card with the appointment date, the doctor who made it, the suggested room (the room of the visit that created the appointment) and the note “… day(s) late” if the date has passed. Clinical content (diagnosis, doctor’s advice) is not shown. 4.2. The Receptionist asks the patient why they came. 4.3. If the patient comes for the follow-up, the Receptionist clicks “Đến tái khám”. The system selects the suggested room and sets the reception type to “Tái khám”. The Receptionist can still change the room, or undo with “Bỏ gắn” until step 11\. 4.4. If the patient comes for another problem, the Receptionist clicks “Khám vấn đề khác”; the reception type stays “Khám bệnh” and the appointment stays Scheduled. 4.5. At step 12, if the visit is linked, the system also sets the appointment to Arrived and links it to the new visit in the same transaction (BR-34). 4.6. The use case continues at step 4\. 5.AF-05 (at step 3): The patient has a follow-up appointment on a later date 5.1. The system shows only the note “Có lịch hẹn tái khám ngày …”, without the “Đến tái khám” button. 5.2. The visit is registered as “Khám bệnh” and the appointment stays Scheduled (BR-34). 5.3. The use case continues at step 4\. 6.AF-06 (at AF-04 step 4.2): The patient no longer needs the follow-up 6.1. The Receptionist clicks “Bệnh nhân không tái khám nữa” and enters a reason. 6.2. The system sets the appointment to Cancelled with the reason, then the use case continues at step 4 as a normal visit, or ends if the patient does not want to register. 7.AF-07 (at step 10): The Receptionist goes back 7.1. The Receptionist clicks “Quay lại”; the entered data is kept. 7.2. The use case returns to step 4\. 8.AF-08 (at step 11): The patient does not agree with the fee 8.1. The Receptionist changes the visit type or room and the use case returns to step 5, or clicks “Hủy” and the use case ends without creating anything. 9.AF-09 (after step 16): The self-paid patient pays 9.1. When the Cashier confirms the receipt (UC-71), the visit becomes Waiting and joins the examination waiting list with the queue number issued at registration, even if patients with later numbers have already paid (BR-15, BR-18). 9.2. The use case ends. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | 1.EF-01 (at step 2 or 12): The patient already has an active visit 1.1. The system shows MSG22; nothing is created. 1.2. The use case ends. 2.EF-02 (at step 10): A required field is missing or too long 2.1. The system shows MSG02 or MSG08 at the field. 2.2. The use case returns to the step of that field. 3.EF-03 (at step 8 or 12): No suitable room 3.1. No active examination room has an assigned doctor, or the selected room has just become unavailable. The system shows MSG56 (BR-07). 3.2. The use case returns to step 9, or ends if no room is available. 4.EF-04 (at step 12): The appointment was just linked to another visit 4.1. The appointment is no longer Scheduled. The system shows MSG91 and nothing is created. 4.2. The use case returns to step 3 with the follow-up card refreshed. 5.EF-05 (at steps 12–14): Session expired or system error 5.1. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; nothing is created. 5.2. The use case returns to step 11\. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the visit and a Pending examination fee receipt exist. A linked follow-up appointment is Arrived. A self-paid patient joins the waiting list after paying; an insurance patient joins immediately and pays after conclusion (BR-15). An unpaid self-paid visit is Abandoned at the end of the day (BR-22). Failure or cancelled: nothing is created, except an appointment cancelled under AF-06. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-07, BR-09, BR-11, BR-12, BR-13, BR-14, BR-15, BR-16, BR-17, BR-18, BR-22, BR-27, BR-36, BR-45, BR-50 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG08, MSG12, MSG16, MSG20, MSG21, MSG22, MSG56, MSG99 |  |  |

### **8.2 UC-41: Print Examination Ticket** {#8.2-uc-41:-print-examination-ticket}

| Primary Actors | Receptionist | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Receptionist, I want to print the examination ticket, so that the patient knows the queue number, the examination room and its location and, if a fee is payable, the amount to pay at the cashier counter (BR-16). Included in UC-40 (step 15). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The visit has been created (UC-40) and has a queue number. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The system builds the ticket (PF-01): hospital name, registration code, patient code, full name, year of birth, gender, queue number (large), examination room name and location, doctor(s) of the room, visit type, coverage rate, priority mark, registration time. 2\. If the patient amount of the examination fee is greater than 0, the system adds the amount to pay and the instruction "Pay at the cashier counter before going to the waiting area" (BR-16). 3\. The system sends the ticket to the ticket printer (HW-01) and shows a preview. 4\. The Receptionist hands the ticket to the patient. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The examination fee is covered (patient amount 0\)** 1\. The ticket shows "Fee covered – go to the waiting area" instead of the amount to pay (BR-15). *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* **AF-02 (at step 1): Reprint (started from UC-36)** 1\. The Receptionist clicks Reprint Ticket on the patient's active visit. 2\. The ticket shows the same data with the mark "Reprint"; if the patient was transferred (UC-48), it shows the current room and queue number. The reprint is recorded in the audit log. *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 3): The printer fails** 1\. The system shows MSG52. The visit is kept; the Receptionist fixes the printer and reprints (AF-02). *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at AF-02 step 1): The visit is closed** 1\. The Reprint button is not shown for Completed or Abandoned visits. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient holds the ticket to pay the examination fee at the cashier (unless covered) and then wait at the room. End of BF-01 on the reception side. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-14, BR-15, BR-16 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG52 |  |  |

### **8.3 UC-42: View Room Queue Status** {#8.3-uc-42:-view-room-queue-status}

| Primary Actors | Receptionist | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Receptionist, I want to see, for each examination room, the assigned doctors and the number of waiting and in-progress patients, so that I can assign new patients to a suitable room with a reasonable waiting time. Used at step 8 of UC-40 and on the Receptionist Dashboard. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Receptionist is signed in (UC-01). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Receptionist opens Room Overview (or reaches step 8 of UC-40). 2\. The system shows each Active examination room grouped by department: room code and name, location, assigned doctors (academic title \+ full name), and today's counts: Waiting for Payment, Waiting, Skipped, In Examination, Waiting for Paraclinical, Waiting for Conclusion. 3\. The system refreshes the counts automatically at least every 10 seconds (UI-04). 4\. The Receptionist clicks a room. 5\. The system shows the room's examination waiting list (Room Detail): queue number, patient name, priority mark, registration time, status, ordered by priority first, then registration time (BR-18). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): A room has no assigned doctor** 1\. The system shows the room greyed out with "No doctor assigned"; it cannot be selected in UC-40. *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* **AF-02 (at step 5): Back to the overview** 1\. The Receptionist clicks Back. *\=\>Return to step 2\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): No room can receive patients** 1\. The system shows MSG56; registration cannot continue and the Receptionist informs the Admin. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 2): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The queue status of the rooms is shown. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-05, BR-07, BR-18; Permission Matrix 4.4 (Waiting list / Queue – View) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG56, MSG99 |  |  |

### **8.4 UC-74: Verify Health Insurance** {#8.4-uc-74:-verify-health-insurance}

| Primary Actors | Receptionist | Secondary Actors | Simulated Health Insurance Portal (BHXH) |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | Là lễ tân, tôi muốn hệ thống tra cứu thẻ BHYT của bệnh nhân qua cổng BHYT mô phỏng, để chỉ áp dụng bảo hiểm cho thẻ hợp lệ với đúng mức hưởng. Nếu thẻ không hợp lệ, lượt khám được đăng ký dạng tự trả và tôi thông báo cho bệnh nhân (BR-13). Cổng là dịch vụ mô phỏng, không kết nối thật với cổng quốc gia (SW-01). Mở rộng UC-40 (bước 6). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | Đăng ký khám (UC-40) đang thực hiện, đã chọn BHYT và đã nhập mã thẻ (10 chữ số hoặc 15 ký tự). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | Hệ thống kiểm tra định dạng mã thẻ (BR-50): đúng 10 chữ số, hoặc đúng 15 ký tự gồm 2 chữ in hoa và 13 chữ số. Hệ thống xác định mã BHXH 10 số: thẻ 10 số thì lấy nguyên; thẻ 15 ký tự thì lấy 10 ký tự cuối. Hệ thống gửi mã BHXH sang cổng mô phỏng. Cổng tra cứu theo mã BHXH và trả về: mã kết quả, trạng thái thẻ, họ tên, ngày sinh (kèm loại ngày sinh), giới tính, số thẻ đang lưu, hiệu lực từ ngày, hiệu lực đến ngày, nơi đăng ký KCB ban đầu (mã 5 số và tên), mức hưởng (%). Hệ thống kiểm tra cổng trả kết quả thành công và thẻ đang hoạt động. Hệ thống đối chiếu họ tên và ngày sinh cổng trả về với hồ sơ bệnh nhân: Họ tên: không phân biệt chữ hoa, chữ thường, bỏ khoảng trắng thừa. Ngày sinh: loại đầy đủ thì so cả ngày-tháng-năm; loại chỉ có tháng-năm thì so tháng và năm; loại chỉ có năm thì so năm. Hệ thống kiểm tra thẻ có hiệu lực tại ngày đăng ký (hiệu lực từ ≤ hôm nay ≤ hiệu lực đến). Hệ thống lấy mức hưởng do cổng trả về để tính các khoản thu của lượt khám (BR-27). Hệ thống hiển thị MSG16 kèm ngày hết hạn và mức hưởng, đồng thời lưu vào lượt khám: mã thẻ đã nhập, mã BHXH, hiệu lực từ/đến, nơi đăng ký KCB ban đầu và mức hưởng. Tiếp tục ở UC-40 bước 7\. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | None |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (tại bước 1): Sai định dạng 1.1 Hệ thống hiển thị MSG05 dưới ô mã thẻ. 1.2 Quay lại UC-40 bước 6\. EF-02 (tại bước 5 hoặc 7): Không tìm thấy thẻ, thẻ không hoạt động (hết hạn, bị thu hồi) hoặc chưa đến ngày hiệu lực 2.1 Hệ thống hiển thị MSG17. Loại lượt khám chuyển sang Tự trả và lễ tân thông báo cho bệnh nhân (BR-13). 2.2 Tiếp tục ở UC-40 bước 7 (UC-40, AF-02). EF-03 (tại bước 6): Họ tên hoặc ngày sinh không khớp 3.1 Hệ thống hiển thị MSG18 kèm dữ liệu cổng trả về. 3.2 Lễ tân kiểm tra thẻ với bệnh nhân và chọn một trong ba cách: sửa mã thẻ (quay lại UC-40 bước 6), sửa hồ sơ bệnh nhân (UC-38), hoặc chuyển sang Tự trả (UC-40, AF-02). EF-04 (tại bước 3): Cổng không trả lời trong 10 giây 4.1 Hệ thống hiển thị MSG20 với hai nút Thử lại và Tự trả. 4.2 Thử lại để quay lại bước 3; Tự trả theo (UC-40, AF-02). |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Thành công: lượt khám đang đăng ký giữ mã thẻ, mã BHXH, hiệu lực từ/đến, nơi đăng ký KCB ban đầu và mức hưởng, dùng để tách mọi khoản thu của lượt khám thành phần BHYT chi trả và phần bệnh nhân trả (BR-27). Thất bại: không áp dụng bảo hiểm; lượt khám là Tự trả. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-11, BR-13, BR-27, BR-50; Data rules: Valid health insurance only, Payment calculation (I.3.3); SW-01, CI-03 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG05, MSG16, MSG17, MSG18, MSG20 |  |  |

## **9\. Clinical Examination** {#9.-clinical-examination}

### **9.1 UC-43: View Patient Waiting List** {#9.1-uc-43:-view-patient-waiting-list}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | The Doctor views, searches, and filters today's examination visits in their assigned room through four tabs: "Chờ khám", "Đang khám", "Chờ kết luận", and "Vắng mặt". From the waiting tabs, the Doctor can select "Bắt đầu" or "Vắng mặt" (UC-44). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01) with an active account. The Doctor has a valid assignment to an active EXAMINATION room (BR-05, BR-19). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor opens "Quản lý khám bệnh". The system identifies the Doctor's assigned examination room. The system retrieves today's visits with WAITING, IN\_EXAMINATION, or WAITING\_CONCLUSION status, including visits marked Skipped. The system displays four tabs: "Chờ khám" (WAITING), "Đang khám" (IN\_EXAMINATION), "Chờ kết luận" (WAITING\_CONCLUSION), and "Vắng mặt" (Skipped). The default tab is "Chờ khám". The system displays: queue number, patient name/code, age, sex, examination type, registration time, notes, status, and actions. Priority and transfer information are combined in "Ghi chú". The "Chờ khám" list is sorted by BR-18: priority patients first, transferred patients second, and regular patients last. The Doctor may search by patient name/code or insurance-card number, filter by priority/examination type, switch tabs, and select page size. For eligible WAITING or WAITING\_CONCLUSION visits, the system displays two actions: "Bắt đầu" and "Vắng mặt" (UC-44). The system automatically refreshes the list every 10 seconds, updating patient counts and information without changing visit statuses. The use case ends when the Doctor leaves the screen or proceeds to UC-44. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 3): No visits. The system displays an empty list and MSG01; automatic refreshing continues. AF-02 (at step 4): "Đang khám". The system displays IN\_EXAMINATION visits without "Bắt đầu"/"Vắng mặt" actions. AF-03 (at step 4): "Chờ kết luận". The system displays WAITING\_CONCLUSION visits with "Bắt đầu"/"Vắng mặt" actions (UC-44). AF-04 (at step 4): "Vắng mặt". The system displays Skipped visits, retaining their interrupted stage. Eligible patients can be re-accepted through UC-46. AF-05 (at step 7): No matching results. The system displays MSG01 and retains filters; the Doctor may modify or clear them. AF-06 (at step 8): Outside a valid shift. Viewing remains available, but attendance actions are blocked (MSG48). |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 2): Invalid room assignment. The system displays ROOM\_ASSIGNMENT\_REQUIRED and prevents access to other rooms. EF-02 (at steps 3 or 9): Loading error. The system displays MSG80 and allows retry. EF-03 (at any step): Session expired. The system displays MSG12 and redirects to UC-01. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: The Doctor views the assigned room's examination visits with appropriate sorting, filters, statuses, and actions. Failure: Viewing, searching, filtering, and refreshing do not modify visit statuses. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-14, BR-15, BR-18, BR-19, BR-21, BR-41, BR-55 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG48, MSG80, MSG99.  |  |  |

### **9.2 UC-44: Handle Patient Call** {#9.2-uc-44:-handle-patient-call}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | The Doctor confirms patient attendance directly from UC-43 using two actions: "Bắt đầu" (START) or "Vắng mặt" (SKIP), without a confirmation dialog. PRESENT proceeds to the appropriate examination or conclusion stage. SKIP marks the patient as absent while preserving the current stage for re-acceptance through UC-46.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01) with an active account.  The Doctor has a valid assignment to an active EXAMINATION room (BR-05, BR-19).  The Doctor is working during a valid shift (BR-19, BR-55).  The visit belongs to the assigned room, has WAITING or WAITING\_CONCLUSION status, and is not marked Skipped. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | From UC-43, the Doctor clicks "Bắt đầu" on a patient. The system processes the action directly without opening a confirmation dialog. The system verifies the Doctor's active account, assigned examination room, and valid shift. The system checks the latest visit status, assigned room, Skipped flag, and record version to ensure the visit is eligible. The system records the responsible Doctor and processes the visit according to its current stage: WAITING: Assign doctorAccountId, change the status to IN\_EXAMINATION, and record the examination start time. WAITING\_CONCLUSION: Assign doctorAccountId, retain WAITING\_CONCLUSION, and allow the Doctor to proceed to UC-56 without restarting the examination. The system updates updatedAt and version, records the attendance action in the audit log, and saves all changes in one transaction (BR-42). The system displays a success message and refreshes UC-43. Patients from WAITING move to "Đang khám"; patients from WAITING\_CONCLUSION proceed to conclusion. The use case ends successfully. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 1): Patient absent. 1.1. The Doctor clicks "Vắng mặt". The system validates the visit using the checks in steps 2–3. 1.2. The system retains WAITING or WAITING\_CONCLUSION, sets isSkipped=true, and records skippedAt. 1.3. The system updates updatedAt and version, records the SKIP action in the audit log, and saves the changes in one transaction. 1.4. The system displays a success message, removes the patient from the active waiting list, and adds the patient to "Vắng mặt" (UC-45). The original stage is preserved for UC-46. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at steps 2–3): Invalid account, room assignment, or shift. The system rejects the action and displays MSG13, ROOM\_ASSIGNMENT\_REQUIRED, or MSG48, as applicable. EF-02 (at step 3): Visit no longer eligible. If the visit is already Skipped, has an invalid status, or its version has changed, the system rejects the action, displays MSG99, and refreshes the list. EF-03 (at steps 4–5 or AF-01): Save or audit error. The system rolls back the transaction, displays MSG80, and allows retry. EF-04 (at any step): Session expired. The system displays MSG12 and redirects to UC-01. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: "Bắt đầu" moves WAITING visits to IN\_EXAMINATION or continues WAITING\_CONCLUSION visits to conclusion. "Vắng mặt" sets the Skipped flag while preserving the original stage for UC-46. All successful actions are recorded in the audit log. Failure: No partial changes, duplicate processing, or unauthorized status transitions are committed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-18, BR-19, BR-20, BR-21, BR-42, BR-55 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG23, MSG48, MSG54, MSG80, MSG99 |  |  |

### **9.3 UC-45: View Skipped Patient List** {#9.3-uc-45:-view-skipped-patient-list}

| Primary Actors | Doctor, Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | The Doctor views and searches skipped examination visits belonging to their assigned room. This use case applies only to visits in EXAMINATION rooms, excluding skipped paraclinical services. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor has successfully signed in and is not required to change their password (UC-01). The Doctor's account is active. The Doctor is assigned to an active EXAMINATION room (BR-05, BR-19). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor opens "Quản lý khám bệnh" and selects the "Vắng mặt" tab in UC-43. The system identifies the Doctor and their assigned EXAMINATION room. The system retrieves today's visits belonging to the assigned room with isSkipped=true and a retained status of WAITING or WAITING\_CONCLUSION.Note: Skipped is a flag indicating the visit's current attendance state, not a value of VisitStatus. The system displays a table with the same fixed-width columns as UC-43: queue number, "Họ tên", "Mã bệnh nhân", "Tuổi", "Giới tính", "Loại khám", "Thời gian đăng ký", "Ghi chú", "Trạng thái", and "Thao tác". No additional columns are displayed for absence time or interrupted stage. "Trạng thái" displays "Vắng mặt" together with the retained stage: WAITING corresponds to "Chờ khám", and WAITING\_CONCLUSION corresponds to "Chờ kết luận". "Ghi chú" displays priority reasons and the source room according to UC-43. If both are present, they appear on separate lines. Column widths remain fixed, and long text wraps without changing the column width. The system sorts visits by skippedAt in ascending order. If multiple visits have the same skippedAt, they are sorted by ascending queue number (BR-21). The system displays the total number of visits currently marked as Skipped in the assigned room. The Doctor may search by patient name, patient code, or health insurance card number, and filter by examination type or interrupted stage. The system paginates the list while preserving the search criteria, filters, and sorting order when the Doctor navigates between pages. The system displays a "Bắt đầu" button in the "Thao tác" column for each visit eligible for re-acceptance. If the patient has not returned, the Doctor takes no action, and the visit remains in "Vắng mặt". Selecting "Bắt đầu" proceeds to UC-46. No "Vắng" button is displayed in this tab. The system automatically refreshes the list according to UI-04, updating the visit information and total count while preserving the selected tab, current page, search criteria, and filters. If the end-of-day process defined in BR-22 changes a visit to ABANDONED, the system removes that visit from the list during the next refresh. UC-45 does not directly perform end-of-day status transitions. End: The use case ends when the Doctor leaves the screen or selects "Bắt đầu" to proceed to UC-46. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 3): No skipped patients 1.1. The system displays an empty list, sets the total count to zero, and shows MSG01. 1.2. Automatic refreshing continues to detect newly skipped visits. AF-02 (at step 7): No matching search or filter results 2.1. The system displays an empty list while retaining the current search and filter criteria. 2.2. The Doctor may modify the criteria or select "Xóa bộ lọc". AF-03 (at step 7): Clear filters 3.1. The system clears the search input, resets all filters, and returns to the first page. 3.2. The system reloads the complete list using the sorting order defined in step 5\. AF-04 (at step 9): Doctor outside the assigned shift 4.1. The Doctor may still view, search, filter, paginate, and refresh the list. 4.2. The system disables the "Bắt đầu" button. If a request is submitted, UC-46 rejects the action and returns MSG48. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 2): Invalid Doctor account or room assignment 1.1. If the account does not belong to a Doctor or is inactive, the system returns MSG13. 1.2. If the Doctor is not assigned to an active EXAMINATION room, the system returns ROOM\_ASSIGNMENT\_REQUIRED. 1.3. The system does not retrieve data belonging to another room. EF-02 (at step 3 or 10): List loading or refresh failure 2.1. The system returns MSG80. 2.2. If previously loaded data is available, the interface may retain it and display a warning that the information is not up to date. 2.3. The Doctor may retry loading the list. EF-03 (at any step): Session expired 3.1. The system displays MSG12, blocks protected actions, and redirects the Doctor to UC-01. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: The Doctor can view visits with isSkipped=true belonging to their assigned EXAMINATION room. Viewing, searching, filtering, pagination, and refreshing do not modify visit data or statuses. Failure: Patient and visit data remain unchanged, and information belonging to other rooms is not disclosed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-19, BR-21, BR-22, BR-42, BR-55 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12,MSG13, MSG48, MSG80. |  |  |

### **9.4 UC-46: Accept Skipped Patient**  {#9.4-uc-46:-accept-skipped-patient}

| Primary Actors | Doctor, Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | The Doctor re-accepts a skipped patient who has returned to the assigned examination room. The system resumes the visit according to its retained WAITING or WAITING\_CONCLUSION stage. This use case applies only to EXAMINATION visits. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor has successfully signed in and is not required to change their password (UC-01). The Doctor's account is active. The Doctor is assigned to an active EXAMINATION room (BR-05, BR-19). The Doctor is on duty in the assigned room (BR-19, BR-55). The visit appears in the "Vắng mặt" tab (UC-45), has isSkipped=true, and retains WAITING or WAITING\_CONCLUSION status. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | When the patient returns, the Doctor selects "Bắt đầu" on the corresponding row in the "Vắng mặt" tab. The system processes the request immediately without displaying a confirmation dialog. The system identifies the Doctor from the current session and verifies that the account is active. The system verifies that the Doctor is assigned to an active EXAMINATION room and is currently on duty in that room. The system retrieves the latest visit information and verifies that the visit belongs to the assigned room, has isSkipped=true, retains WAITING or WAITING\_CONCLUSION status, and has not been modified by another request. The system re-accepts the visit based on its retained status: WAITING: Set isSkipped=false, clear skippedAt, assign the current Doctor to doctorAccountId, change the status to IN\_EXAMINATION, and record the examination start time. WAITING\_CONCLUSION: Set isSkipped=false, clear skippedAt, retain WAITING\_CONCLUSION and the existing doctorAccountId, and resume the conclusion stage. Note: If a WAITING\_CONCLUSION visit has no assigned doctorAccountId due to invalid data, the system rejects the request instead of automatically assigning another Doctor. The system updates updatedAt and version and creates an ACCEPT\_SKIPPED audit record containing the visit, resumed stage, accepting Doctor, and acceptance time. The system saves the visit changes and audit record within a single transaction. The system confirms successful processing and refreshes UC-43/UC-45: From WAITING: The visit is removed from "Vắng mặt", appears in "Đang khám", and the Doctor proceeds to UC-47. From WAITING\_CONCLUSION: The visit is removed from "Vắng mặt", and the Doctor resumes the corresponding conclusion stage without repeating the examination. End: The use case ends when the transaction is successfully committed. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 1): Patient has not returned 1.1. The Doctor takes no action. 1.2. The visit remains in "Vắng mặt" with isSkipped=true, its existing skippedAt, and its retained status unchanged. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 2): Unauthorized or inactive Doctor account 1.1. If the account does not belong to a Doctor or is inactive, the system rejects the request and returns MSG13. 1.2. No changes are saved. EF-02 (at step 3): Invalid room assignment or Doctor outside the assigned shift 2.1. If the Doctor is not assigned to an active EXAMINATION room, the system returns ROOM\_ASSIGNMENT\_REQUIRED. 2.2. If the Doctor is not on duty in the assigned room, the system rejects the request and returns MSG48. EF-03 (at step 4): Visit belongs to another room 3.1. The system rejects the request and returns MSG13. 3.2. The system neither modifies nor discloses data belonging to another room. EF-04 (at step 4 or 5): Visit no longer eligible for re-acceptance 4.1. The system rejects the request if isSkipped is no longer true, the visit status is no longer WAITING or WAITING\_CONCLUSION, the visit has changed to ABANDONED, or a WAITING\_CONCLUSION visit has no assigned Doctor. 4.2. The system returns MSG99 and refreshes the list. 4.3. No changes are saved. EF-05 (at step 4 or 7): Duplicate request or version conflict 5.1. If the optimistic version is no longer valid, the system rolls back the transaction and returns MSG99. 5.2. The system refreshes the list before allowing the Doctor to retry. EF-06 (at step 5, 6, or 7): Data persistence or audit logging failure 6.1. The system rolls back the entire transaction and returns MSG80. 6.2. The visit retains its previous isSkipped, skippedAt, and status. EF-07 (at any step): Session expired 7.1. The system displays MSG12, blocks the action, and redirects the Doctor to UC-01. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: The visit is removed from the Skipped list and resumes its appropriate stage. WAITING transitions to IN\_EXAMINATION, while WAITING\_CONCLUSION resumes the conclusion process. The accepting Doctor, acceptance time, and resumed stage are recorded in the audit log. Failure: The visit retains its previously saved state. No partial updates, duplicate acceptance, or unauthorized modifications to visits belonging to other rooms occur. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-19, BR-20, BR-21,BR-42, BR-55 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG13, MSG48, MSG80, MSG99. |  |  |

### **9.5 UC-47: Perform Clinical Examination** {#9.5-uc-47:-perform-clinical-examination}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | The Doctor performs a clinical examination for a patient whose attendance has been confirmed at the assigned room. The system displays the current outpatient medical record following the structure of Form 15/BV1. The Doctor records the reason for visit, present-illness history, medical and allergy history, vital signs, general and organ-system findings, and a preliminary diagnosis. Preliminary-diagnosis text is mandatory before ordering paraclinical services; an ICD-10 code is optional at this stage, but any selected code must be active (BR-23, BR-31, BR-51, BR-98–BR-100). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01), assigned to a valid examination room, and working the current shift (BR-05, BR-19, BR-55). The patient's attendance has been confirmed and examination started through UC-44. The visit is "In Examination" and assigned to this Doctor. The current visit's medical record has not been closed or locked (BR-32, BR-35). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | Following UC-44 attendance confirmation, the Doctor opens "Clinical Examination" for the current visit. The system checks permission, assigned room, shift, and visit/record status (BR-02, BR-05, BR-19, BR-32, BR-55; MSG13/MSG48/MSG68 as applicable). The system retrieves patient profile, visit information, medical history, allergies, and previously saved examination data. The system displays patient and visit details: name/code; birth date, age and sex; occupation, ethnicity and address; visit type and insurance-card number if applicable; visit code, ticket number and date; queue number, room and Doctor; current visit status. The clinical-examination form follows outpatient Form 15/BV1: "II. Reason for Admission"; "III. Medical Interview"; "IV. Examination"; "Preliminary Diagnosis"; and "Treatment/Care Performed" where applicable. The system prepopulates the reception-recorded reason for visit; the Doctor may supplement it. Its length must be 2–1,000 characters (BR-95). The Doctor records the present-illness course (symptom progression and current condition); this field is optional, maximum 4,000 characters (BR-99). Existing medical history and allergies are displayed. The Doctor may update personal history, family history, drug allergies, and notes through UC-39 under BR-23 and BR-93. Only the Doctor may make these clinical-history changes during examination. The "Vital Signs" area includes pulse, temperature, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, respiratory rate, weight, height, SpO2, BMI calculated from weight and height when available, measurement time, and measurer. The Doctor reviews existing measurements or enters required additional measurements. Validation follows BR-98: each individual measure may be blank, but at least one valid vital-sign value is required when saving; pulse 20–250 bpm; temperature 30.0–45.0 °C; respiratory rate 5–80/min; systolic pressure 50–300 mmHg; diastolic pressure 20–200 mmHg and less than systolic; weight 0.5–300 kg; height 30–250 cm; SpO2 50–100%. The Doctor may enter general examination findings (optional, maximum 4,000 characters; BR-99). The Doctor records organ-system findings as needed under: cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, renal/urinary, neurological, musculoskeletal, ear/nose/throat, and endocrine/nutritional/other. For each organ finding, the organ group is mandatory; finding text must be 2–2,000 characters; optional notes are limited to 500 characters (BR-99). The Doctor enters a textual "Preliminary Diagnosis" based on history and findings. The system permits searching/selecting an active ICD-10 code: the code is optional at this stage (BR-100); when selected it is validated under BR-31/BR-46/BR-51 and the code plus diagnosis name are saved as a snapshot. The Doctor records any treatment or care already performed. The Doctor chooses "Save Draft", "Save and Continue", or "Cancel". On save, the system validates fields relevant to the chosen action, including formatting, vital signs, and a valid preliminary-diagnosis text before proceeding to paraclinical ordering. The system saves clinical data into the current visit's medical record, with the responsible Doctor and update time. Changes to clinical records are audited under BR-42, including user, timestamp, and before/after values where relevant. The system displays MSG03 or an appropriate save-success notice. With "Save and Continue", the system proceeds to UC-49 if paraclinical tests are needed or UC-56 if sufficient information exists for conclusion. The visit and medical record remain active; examination alone does not mark the visit Completed. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 19): Save Draft. 1.1. The Doctor clicks "Save Draft"; the system validates formats and BR-98 vital-sign rules but allows preliminary-diagnosis text to remain blank until a transition that requires it. 1.2. The system saves valid entered data, shows MSG03, and keeps the visit "In Examination". AF-02 (at step 9): Update medical history/allergies. 2.1. The Doctor opens UC-39, edits the relevant history/allergy data, and saves under BR-23/BR-93, with BR-42 audit where required. 2.2. The examination screen refreshes the details; resume step 10\. AF-03 (at step 10): No vital signs yet. 3.1. The form displays empty fields; the Doctor enters at least one valid vital sign and records the actual measurer/time. Continue at step 12\. AF-04 (at step 24): Order paraclinical services. 4.1. Before allowing UC-49, validate preliminary-diagnosis text of 2–1,000 characters (BR-100; show MSG98 if invalid). An initial ICD-10 code is not required. 4.2. Save the examination data and proceed to UC-49; keep the medical record open for later review. AF-05 (at step 24): No paraclinical services required. 5.1. Save examination data and proceed to conclusion (UC-56), governed by BR-30/BR-32. AF-06 (at step 19): Cancel/leave with unsaved changes. 6.1. Show MSG38 if changes are unsaved. If the Doctor continues editing, preserve the form; if discarding, remove only unsaved changes and retain previously saved data. AF-07 (at step 17): No ICD-10 code selected. 7.1. Accept valid preliminary-diagnosis text without an ICD-10 code (BR-100); do not assign a code automatically. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at step 20): Missing required information. 1.1. Display MSG02 next to the relevant field, reject the invalid save/transition, and return to step 19\. EF-02 (at step 12): Invalid vital signs. 2.1. Show MSG96 when no vital-sign value is provided at save time, or MSG97 with the relevant rule when values are out of range or diastolic is not below systolic. Reject invalid values and return to step 11\. EF-03 (at steps 15 or 20): Invalid organ finding. 3.1. For a missing organ group/content or excessive text, show MSG02 or MSG08 as appropriate; return to step 14 for correction. EF-04 (at step 24): Invalid/missing preliminary diagnosis before paraclinical ordering. 4.1. Block UC-49, display MSG98 at the diagnosis field, and return to step 16\. EF-05 (at step 17): Inactive or invalid ICD-10 code. 5.1. Prevent selection and show an unavailable-code notice; the Doctor may select another active code or leave the code blank under BR-100. EF-06 (at steps 2 or 21): Medical record already closed/locked. 6.1. Display MSG68, prevent editing, and end the use case (BR-32). EF-07 (at steps 2 or 21): Doctor lacks permission or is outside the assigned room/shift. 7.1. Display MSG13 or MSG48 as appropriate, prevent updates, and end. EF-08 (at any step): Session expired. 8.1. Display MSG12, redirect to UC-01, and end. EF-09 (at steps 3–22): System/network failure. 9.1. Display MSG80; never claim success before persistence. The Doctor may reload and retry after checking the current data. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: History/allergy updates, vital signs, examination findings, and preliminary diagnosis are saved in the current visit's outpatient medical record. Relevant changes are recorded in the audit log. The record remains open until conclusion is confirmed under BR-32. Failure: Invalid data is not saved, and previously persisted data is retained. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-19, BR-23, BR-30, BR-31, BR-32, BR-35, BR-42, BR-46, BR-51, BR-55, BR-93, BR-95, BR-98, BR-99, BR-100 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG03, MSG08, MSG12, MSG13, MSG38, MSG40, MSG48, MSG68, MSG80, MSG96, MSG97, MSG98 |  |  |

### **9.6 UC-48: Transfer Patient to Another Room** {#9.6-uc-48:-transfer-patient-to-another-room}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | During a valid shift, the Doctor may transfer a patient of their room who is waiting for examination or has been called but whose current-visit medical record has not yet been opened. The destination must be a different active examination room with a Doctor scheduled that day. A transfer reason is mandatory. The system retains the same visit, issues the next queue number for the destination room, marks "Transferred from room ...", and places the patient after priority patients but before ordinary patients. After a successful transfer, the new queue number is shown and the examination ticket may be reprinted; no additional examination fee is charged (BR-18, BR-24, BR-96, BR-97). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | The Doctor is signed in (UC-01), assigned to an examination room, and working a valid shift (BR-05, BR-19, BR-55). The patient belongs to the Doctor's room and is waiting for examination, or was called but the current-visit medical record has not been opened. The visit has not been completed or abandoned. Note: The existence of an eligible destination room is checked in the Normal/Alternative Flow, not assumed as a precondition (AF-03, BR-96). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | The Doctor opens the examination-waiting list (UC-43) or a called patient's details before opening the medical record (UC-44). The Doctor selects an eligible patient and clicks "Transfer Room". The system checks the latest visit status, source room, shift, and whether the medical record has already been opened (MSG56 if opened; MSG99 if status changed). The "Transfer Examination Room" screen displays patient name/code, birth date, sex, visit type and insurance card if applicable, visit date/code, current room, current queue number, reason for visit, and visit status. The transfer form provides required "Destination Room" and "Transfer Reason" fields, optional "Notes", and "Cancel"/"Confirm Transfer" buttons. The system retrieves eligible rooms under BR-07/BR-96: different from the source, active, with a Doctor scheduled that day, and otherwise eligible to accept the patient. The system lists eligible rooms with code, name, department, location, and scheduled Doctor information where available. The Doctor selects a destination room. The system displays its details and permits entry of the transfer reason. The Doctor enters a reason of 5–500 characters (BR-97); MSG100 applies if the length is invalid. The Doctor may add optional notes. The Doctor clicks "Confirm Transfer". The system rechecks that: (a) the patient remains assigned to the source room; (b) the visit is neither completed nor abandoned; (c) the patient is waiting or has been called without opening the record; (d) the destination differs from the source, is active, and has a Doctor scheduled that day; (e) the reason has 5–500 characters; and (f) the transferring Doctor is in a valid shift. The system atomically assigns the next non-duplicated queue number in the destination room under BR-18. The system updates the existing visit: destination room and queue number, "Waiting for Examination" status, transfer marker, source room, and transfer time. The system saves transfer history: visit code, source/destination rooms, old/new queue numbers, transfer reason, user, time, and optional notes. The system removes the patient from the source room's waiting list. The system inserts the patient in the destination room's "Waiting for Examination" list with "Transferred from room ...". BR-18 determines placement: after priority patients; within the transfer group by ascending arrival time and then queue number on ties; before ordinary patients. If the patient is also priority, apply the priority group's ordering. The existing visit ID and receipts/fees remain unchanged; transferring rooms creates no additional examination charge (BR-24). The system records the relevant change/audit history. The system displays MSG24 with the destination room and new queue number. The system shows updated visit details and the "Reprint Examination Ticket" action. The use case ends successfully. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | AF-01 (at step 11): Doctor cancels. 1.1. Clicking "Cancel" prompts MSG38 if there are unsaved changes. On confirmed cancellation the screen closes and the room, queue number, and visit status remain unchanged. AF-02 (at step 23): Reprint ticket. 2.1. The Doctor clicks "Reprint Examination Ticket". The system prepares a ticket using the existing visit ID, new queue number, destination room, and location, then continues with UC-41. 2.2. Reprinting creates neither a new visit nor a new examination charge. AF-03 (at step 6): No eligible destination room. 3.1. If no other room meets BR-96, the system displays an explanatory notice, disables "Confirm Transfer", and keeps the patient in the source room. AF-04 (at step 3): Patient called, record not opened. 4.1. The system permits transfer under BR-24. After transfer, the visit becomes "Waiting for Examination" in the destination and no longer remains in "Calling" status in the source room. AF-05 (at step 11): No optional note. 5.1. The system accepts a blank note and continues at step 12\. |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | EF-01 (at steps 3 or 13): Medical record already opened. 1.1. The system displays MSG56, rejects transfer, and retains the original room/queue/status. EF-02 (at steps 10 or 13): Missing transfer reason. 2.1. The system displays MSG31; the Doctor supplies the reason and returns to step 10\. EF-03 (at step 13): Transfer reason violates BR-97. 3.1. The system displays MSG100 for fewer than 5 or more than 500 characters, blocks confirmation, and returns to step 10\. EF-04 (at step 13): Destination room no longer eligible. 4.1. If the destination is inactive, lacks a Doctor scheduled that day, or fails an acceptance condition, display MSG53 and allow a different selection (return to step 8). EF-05 (at step 13): Visit is no longer transferable. 5.1. If it has already transferred, been skipped, completed, abandoned, or otherwise changed contrary to BR-24, reject transfer, show MSG99, reload details, and end. EF-06 (at steps 13–16): Concurrent transfer or queue-number conflict. 6.1. Prevent duplicate queue numbers and repeat transfers. If an atomic transaction cannot complete, roll back all partial changes; show MSG99 for a changed visit, or MSG80 for a system transaction failure. The Doctor may reload and retry if still eligible. EF-07 (at step 23): Reprint fails. 7.1. Display MSG49, retain the successful transfer, and allow a retry. EF-08 (at steps 3 or 13): Doctor outside a valid shift. 8.1. Display MSG48 and reject the transfer. EF-09 (at any step): Session expired. 9.1. Display MSG12 and redirect to UC-01. EF-10 (at steps 3–22): System/network error. 10.1. Display MSG80. If transfer was not committed, preserve the previous room and queue; never report success before confirmation. Allow refresh and retry. |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: The patient belongs to an eligible destination examination room with a new queue number and "Transferred from room ..." marker, ordered under BR-18. Transfer history is saved; the visit ID and payment records are retained, no additional examination fee arises, and a reprinted ticket is available. Failure: No invalid transfer is created and an unsuccessful transaction does not alter the previously saved room, queue number, or visit status. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-02, BR-05, BR-07, BR-18, BR-19, BR-24, BR-42, BR-53, BR-55, BR-96, BR-97 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG08, MSG12, MSG31, MSG38, MSG48, MSG49, MSG53, MSG56, MSG80, MSG99, MSG100 |  |  |

### **9.7 UC-49: Order Paraclinical Services** {#9.7-uc-49:-order-paraclinical-services}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | Cashier (collects the paraclinical fee afterwards) |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to select paraclinical services, review the estimated cost with the patient and confirm the order, so that a paraclinical receipt is created and, once paid, the services are routed to the paraclinical rooms (BR-25, BR-26, BR-28). Only active services can be ordered (BR-10). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The visit is In Examination by the Doctor and its medical record is open (UC-47), or the Doctor is reviewing results before the conclusion and the record is not closed (UC-56, more tests needed). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor clicks Order Paraclinical Services. 2\. The system shows the active paraclinical services grouped by type and group (Lab, Imaging, Functional) with a search box, the clinic price and insurance price of each service (BR-08, BR-10). 3\. The Doctor selects one or more services and may add a clinical note for the technician. 4\. The system shows the estimated cost per service and in total, split into the insurance amount and the patient amount according to the visit type and coverage rate (BR-27). 5\. The Doctor explains the services and the estimated cost to the patient (BR-25). 6\. The patient agrees; the Doctor clicks Confirm Order. 7\. The system checks that at least one service is selected, that every service is Active and that no service appears twice in the order. 8\. The system creates one paraclinical order per selected service (status Pending Payment) with the current prices stored (BR-09), and one paraclinical receipt (status Pending) with one line per service (BR-26, BR-27). 9\. The system sets the visit to Waiting for Paraclinical, records the order in the audit log and shows MSG67. 10\. The Doctor prints the paraclinical order slip (UC-50) and tells the patient to pay at the cashier counter. The receipt appears in the Cashier's waiting payment list (UC-69). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 8): The patient amount of the receipt is 0** 1\. The system sets the receipt to Paid automatically and releases the orders immediately: each order becomes Waiting and is routed to the Active room with the fewest waiting patients among the rooms that perform the service (BR-26, BR-28). 2\. The order slip shows the assigned rooms. *\=\>Continue at step 9\.* **AF-02 (at step 6): The patient does not agree before the order is confirmed** 1\. The Doctor does not confirm; no order or receipt is created. The Doctor records the refusal in the findings (UC-47, AF-03). *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-03 (at step 3): An insured patient selects a service outside insurance coverage** 1\. The system marks the service "Not covered"; it is charged at the clinic price and the patient still pays it (BR-26, BR-27). *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* **AF-04 (at step 1): Additional tests after reviewing results (from UC-56)** 1\. The visit goes back from Waiting for Conclusion to Waiting for Paraclinical when the new order is confirmed; a new receipt is created for the new services. *\=\>Continue at step 2\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 7): No service selected or duplicate service** 1\. The system shows MSG02 or MSG07. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 7): A selected service was deactivated meanwhile** 1\. The system shows MSG42 and removes the service from the selection. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-03 (at step 8): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; no order or receipt is created (all or nothing). *\=\>Return to step 6\.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the orders and the paraclinical receipt exist. The orders reach the paraclinical rooms only after the receipt is Paid (UC-71) or immediately if the patient amount is 0 (BR-26). A confirmed order cannot be cancelled by the Doctor; if the receipt is still unpaid at the end of the day, it becomes Cancelled together with its orders and the visit becomes Abandoned (BR-22, BR-25). Failure / Cancelled: no order and no receipt are created. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-08, BR-09, BR-10, BR-19, BR-22, BR-25, BR-26, BR-27, BR-28; Data rules: Paraclinical order content, Price snapshot (I.3.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG07, MSG12, MSG42, MSG67, MSG99 |  |  |

### **9.8 UC-50: Print Paraclinical Order** {#9.8-uc-50:-print-paraclinical-order}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to print the paraclinical order slip showing the ordered services and where each one is performed, so that the patient knows where to pay and where to go. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Doctor has confirmed a paraclinical order (UC-49). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor clicks Print Order (or the system opens the print preview after UC-49). 2\. The system builds the slip (PF-02): hospital name, patient code and name, year of birth, gender, registration code, visit type and coverage rate, order date, ordering Doctor, clinical note, and for each service: service name, performing department and location, insurance amount and patient amount; total patient amount and the instruction "Pay at the cashier counter". 3\. The system sends the slip to the office printer (HW-02) and shows a preview. 4\. The Doctor hands the slip to the patient. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The orders are already released (fee paid or patient amount 0\)** 1\. The slip shows the assigned room and location of each service instead of the payment instruction (BR-28). *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* **AF-02 (at step 1): Reprint** 1\. The Doctor opens the order from the Current Visit Record and clicks Print; the slip is marked "Reprint" and shows the current status and assigned room of each service. *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 3): The printer fails** 1\. The system shows MSG52; the order is not affected. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient holds the order slip. No data is changed (the print is recorded in the audit log). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-26, BR-27, BR-28 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG52 |  |  |

## **10\. Medical Record** {#10.-medical-record}

### **10.1 UC-51: View List Medical Record** {#10.1-uc-51:-view-list-medical-record}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to search and view the list of medical records of patients, so that I can review their examination history. Doctors can view the medical records of all patients (BR-35). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Doctor is signed in (UC-01). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor selects Medical Records in the menu. 2\. The system shows the search box (patient code, citizen ID, name, phone) and filters: Visit date (From – To), Room, Diagnosis (ICD-10), Status (Completed, Abandoned, Active). 3\. The Doctor enters a keyword and/or filters. 4\. The system shows the matching patients: patient code, full name, date of birth, gender, number of visits, last visit date, last diagnosis. 5\. The Doctor selects a patient. 6\. The system shows the list of visits of the patient, newest first: registration code, date, room, doctor, visit type, final diagnosis (ICD-10), status. 7\. The Doctor selects a visit. *\=\>Continue in UC-52.* |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 1): Opened from the current visit** 1\. From the Current Visit Record (UC-47), the Doctor clicks History; the system opens step 6 for the patient of the visit. *\=\>Continue at step 6\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 4): No record matches** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 1): The user is not a Doctor** 1\. The system shows MSG13. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-03 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The medical records are listed. No data is changed. Every access to a patient's records is recorded in the audit log. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-35; Data rule: Medical data is access-controlled (I.3.3); Security: Medical data confidentiality (IV.2.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG13, MSG99 |  |  |

### **10.2 UC-52: View Medical Record Detail** {#10.2-uc-52:-view-medical-record-detail}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to view the detail of a medical record, including the examination history and the paraclinical results of all visits, so that I can make decisions based on the patient's full history (BR-35). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Doctor has selected a visit in UC-51, UC-34 or from the Current Visit Record (UC-47). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The system shows the patient header: patient code, full name, age, gender, drug allergies (red label), medical history. 2\. The system shows the selected visit: registration code, date, room, doctor, visit type, priority, reason and initial symptoms, transfers (if any), vital signs, symptoms and findings, paraclinical orders with results and files (UC-55), final diagnosis (ICD-10) and conclusion, prescription, follow-up appointment, status and closed time. 3\. The Doctor can switch to another visit of the same patient with the visit timeline. 4\. The Doctor clicks a result file to open it; the system checks the Doctor's access before every download (Data rule: Medical data is access-controlled, I.3.3). 5\. The system shows the action Export Medical Record (UC-53). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The visit is the Doctor's current, unfinished visit** 1\. The system shows the Edit button, which opens the Current Visit Record (UC-47 / UC-56). Records of other visits are read-only (BR-35). *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* **AF-02 (at step 2): The visit is Abandoned** 1\. The system shows the data recorded before the visit was abandoned, marked "Abandoned – no conclusion" (BR-22). *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): The record does not exist** 1\. The system shows MSG41. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 4): The file cannot be loaded** 1\. The system shows MSG99. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-03 (any step): Session expired** 1\. The system shows MSG12. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The medical record is shown read-only (except the current unfinished visit). The access is recorded in the audit log. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-22, BR-32, BR-35; Data rule: Medical data is access-controlled (I.3.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG41, MSG99 |  |  |

### **10.3 UC-53: Export Medical Record** {#10.3-uc-53:-export-medical-record}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to export a medical record to a printable file, so that it can be printed or stored according to the hospital's needs. Doctors can export the records of all patients (BR-35). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Doctor is viewing a medical record (UC-52). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor clicks Export Medical Record. 2\. The system asks for the scope: Current visit only, or All visits of the patient. 3\. The Doctor selects the scope and confirms. 4\. The system creates a PDF file (SW-03) using the medical record layout (patient information, visits with vital signs, findings, paraclinical results, diagnosis, prescription, follow-up), with the hospital header, export time and exporting Doctor. 5\. The system downloads the file and shows MSG36. 6\. The system records the export in the audit log (patient, scope, Doctor, time). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 3): The Doctor cancels** 1\. No file is created. *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-02 (at step 4): The visit is not closed yet** 1\. The file is marked "Draft – visit not completed". *\=\>Continue at step 5\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 4): The file cannot be created** 1\. The system shows MSG99. *\=\>Return to step 2\.* **EF-02 (any step): Session expired** 1\. The system shows MSG12. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The file is downloaded and the export is logged. No data in the system is changed. |  |  |
