| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG36, MSG99 |  |  |

## **11\. Examination Conclusion** {#11.-examination-conclusion}

### **11.1 UC-54: View Patients Pending Conclusion** {#11.1-uc-54:-view-patients-pending-conclusion}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to see the patients of my room whose paraclinical results are all available and who are waiting for conclusion, so that I can call them back to conclude the visit. Each examination room has a conclusion waiting list besides the examination waiting list (BR-18). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Doctor is signed in and is assigned to an Active examination room. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor opens the Waiting for Conclusion tab of the waiting list (or Patient Pending Conclusion on the Doctor Dashboard). 2\. The system shows the visits of this room with status Waiting for Conclusion (every paraclinical order of the visit has a result – BR-28, BR-30): queue number, patient name, age, priority mark, ordering Doctor, number of results, time the last result was submitted. 3\. The system orders the list: priority patients first, then by registration time (BR-18). 4\. The system also shows, in a separate read-only section, the visits of the room still Waiting for Paraclinical with their progress (e.g. 2/3 results). 5\. When all results of a visit are submitted, the system moves it to the list automatically and notifies the Doctor (background job 8). 6\. The Doctor clicks Call Next or Call on a patient. *\=\>Continue in UC-44.* |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The list is empty** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* **AF-02 (at step 6): The Doctor wants to look at the results before calling** 1\. The Doctor clicks View Results. *\=\>Continue in UC-55.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The Doctor is not assigned to any room** 1\. The system shows MSG50. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The conclusion waiting list of the room is shown. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-18, BR-19, BR-28, BR-30 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG50, MSG99 |  |  |

### **11.2 UC-55: View Paraclinical Results** {#11.2-uc-55:-view-paraclinical-results}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to view the paraclinical results recorded by the Technicians for the current visit, so that I can conclude based on all ordered results. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Doctor is examining or concluding a visit of their room (UC-44, UC-47), or is viewing a medical record (UC-52). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor opens the Paraclinical Results tab of the Current Visit Record. 2\. The system shows every paraclinical order of the visit: service, room, status (Pending Payment, Waiting, Skipped, In Progress, Performed, Completed, Cancelled), Technician, performed time, result submitted time. 3\. For each Completed order the system shows the result content (values with reference ranges, description), the result conclusion and the attached files (images, PDF). 4\. The Doctor opens a file; the system checks the Doctor's access before every download and shows it in a viewer. 5\. The Doctor reviews the results. *\=\>Continue in UC-56 (or UC-49 if more tests are needed).* |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): Some results are not yet available** 1\. The system marks the missing orders with their current status; the Conclude button stays disabled (BR-30). *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-02 (at step 3): A value is outside its reference range** 1\. The system highlights the value. *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 4): The file cannot be loaded** 1\. The system shows MSG99. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (any step): Session expired** 1\. The system shows MSG12. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The results are shown. No data is changed. Submitted results cannot be edited (BR-29). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-19, BR-29, BR-30, BR-35; Data rule: Medical data is access-controlled (I.3.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG99 |  |  |

### **11.3 UC-56: Conclude Examination** {#11.3-uc-56:-conclude-examination}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to record the final diagnosis (with an ICD-10 code if available) and the conclusion and treatment plan after reviewing all paraclinical results, so that the visit can be completed. The Doctor can only conclude when every paraclinical order of the visit has a result (BR-30, BR-31). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The visit belongs to the Doctor's room and its record is open: either the examination is finished and no paraclinical service was ordered (UC-47), or the patient was called back from the conclusion waiting list (UC-44) and every order has a result. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor opens the Conclusion tab of the Current Visit Record. 2\. The system checks that every paraclinical order of the visit is Completed (BR-30). 3\. The system shows the summary of the visit (vital signs, findings, paraclinical results) and the conclusion form: Final diagnosis\* (primary), ICD-10 code (pick list with search by code or name, optional if no code applies – BR-31), Secondary diagnoses (optional, with ICD-10), Conclusion and treatment plan\*, Advice for the patient. 4\. The Doctor fills in the form and clicks Save Conclusion. 5\. The system checks the required fields and lengths (diagnosis ≤ 500, conclusion ≤ 2,000 characters). 6\. The system saves the conclusion to the medical record and records it in the audit log. 7\. The system shows MSG03 and the next actions: Prescribe Medication (UC-59) if medication is needed, Create Follow-up Appointment (UC-61) for chronic diseases, Print Conclusion (UC-57), Close Medical Record (UC-58). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 3): More paraclinical tests are needed** 1\. The Doctor clicks Order Additional Services. *\=\>Continue in UC-49 (AF-04); the visit goes back to Waiting for Paraclinical.* **AF-02 (at step 4): The Doctor edits the conclusion again before closing** 1\. The conclusion can be changed and saved again as long as the record is not closed (BR-32). *\=\>Return to step 4\.* **AF-03 (at step 1): The patient is absent when called for conclusion** 1\. The visit is moved to the skipped list (UC-44, AF-01); when the patient returns it goes back to Waiting for Conclusion (UC-46). *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): Some paraclinical orders have no result** 1\. The system shows MSG25 with the number of orders without result; the form is disabled. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 5): Required field empty or too long** 1\. The system shows MSG02 or MSG08. *\=\>Return to step 4\.* **EF-03 (at step 6): Session expired or system errorr** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; the entered data stays on the screen. *\=\>Return to step 4\.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the final diagnosis and conclusion are saved in the medical record; the visit is ready for prescription, follow-up, printing and closing. Failure: the conclusion is not saved. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-19, BR-30, BR-31, BR-32 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG03, MSG08, MSG12, MSG25, MSG99 |  |  |

### **11.4 UC-57: Print Conclusion** {#11.4-uc-57:-print-conclusion}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to print the examination conclusion for the patient, so that the patient keeps the result of the visit. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The conclusion of the visit has been saved (UC-56). |  |  |

The system sends the form to the office printer (HW-02) and shows a preview. 4\. The Doctor hands the conclusion to the patient (together with the prescription – UC-60). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 1): Print after closing (reprint)** 1\. The Doctor opens the closed visit from the medical record (UC-52) and prints; the form is marked "Copy". *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The conclusion is not saved yet** 1\. The Print button is disabled and the system shows MSG65. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 3): The printer fails** 1\. The system shows MSG52. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient receives the printed conclusion. No data is changed (the print is logged). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-31, BR-32 |  |  |

### **11.5 UC-58: Close Medical Record** {#11.5-uc-58:-close-medical-record}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to close the medical record after concluding (and prescribing if needed), so that the visit is marked Completed and the record is locked. Since the examination and paraclinical fees were collected in advance, there is no payment after the conclusion (BR-32). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The conclusion of the visit has been saved (UC-56). 2\. The prescription (UC-59) and follow-up appointment (UC-61), if needed, have been saved. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor clicks Close Medical Record. 2\. The system checks that the final diagnosis and conclusion are saved and that every paraclinical order is Completed (BR-30). 3\. The system shows MSG27. 4\. The Doctor confirms. 5\. The system locks the medical record of the visit (vital signs, findings, results, diagnosis, prescription, follow-up appointment can no longer be edited), sets the visit to Completed with the closed time and records it in the audit log. 6\. The system shows MSG03 and removes the visit from the room's lists. 7\. The Doctor hands the printed conclusion and prescription to the patient; the patient buys medication outside the hospital (BR-33). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 4): The Doctor does not confirm** 1\. The record stays open. *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-02 (at step 1): The conclusion and prescription are not printed yet** 1\. The system reminds the Doctor to print them (UC-57, UC-60) before closing; the Doctor may print now or later from the medical record. *\=\>Continue at step 2\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): The conclusion is missing** 1\. The system shows MSG65. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 2): Some paraclinical orders have no result** 1\. The system shows MSG25. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-03 (at step 5): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; the record stays open. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the visit is Completed and its record is locked and cannot be edited by anyone (BR-32). End of BF-04 ("Visit completed"). Failure / Cancelled: the record stays open. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-30, BR-32, BR-33, BR-35 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG03, MSG12, MSG25, MSG27, MSG65, MSG99 |  |  |

### **11.6 UC-59: Prescribe Medication** {#11.6-uc-59:-prescribe-medication}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to create a prescription with drug, quantity, unit and usage instructions, so that the patient can buy the medication outside the hospital. The hospital does not sell or dispense medication: the prescription is only printed for the patient, and receipts never include drug costs (BR-33). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The conclusion of the visit has been saved (UC-56) and the record is not closed. 2\. The Doctor is the examining doctor of the visit. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor clicks Prescribe Medication. 2\. The system shows the prescription form with the patient's diagnosis and drug allergies (red label – BR-23): for each drug line Drug name\* (with strength), Unit\*, Quantity\*, Usage instructions\* (dose, times per day, route, timing), Number of days; plus a general note. 3\. The Doctor adds one or more drug lines and clicks Save. 4\. The system checks that there is at least one drug line, that required fields are filled in and that quantities are whole numbers greater than 0\. 5\. The system checks the drugs against the patient's recorded allergies. 6\. The system saves the electronic prescription to the medical record of the visit (one prescription per visit) and records it in the audit log. 7\. The system shows MSG03 and the actions Print Prescription (UC-60) and Create Follow-up Appointment (UC-61). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 5): A drug matches a recorded allergy** 1\. The system shows MSG26. The Doctor changes the drug (=\>return to step 3\) or confirms that the drug is intended. *\=\>Continue at step 6\.* **AF-02 (at step 3): Edit the prescription before closing** 1\. The Doctor opens the saved prescription, changes lines and saves again (only while the record is not closed – BR-32). *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* **AF-03 (at step 1): No medication is needed** 1\. The Doctor skips this use case. *\=\>Continue in UC-61 or UC-58.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 4): No drug line or required field missing** 1\. The system shows MSG02 or MSG05. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 6): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; the entered data stays on the screen. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the visit has one electronic prescription that will be printed for the patient. No receipt is created for medication (BR-33). Failure: no prescription is saved. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-23, BR-32, BR-33; Data rule: One prescription per examination (I.3.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG03, MSG05, MSG12, MSG26, MSG99 |  |  |

### **11.7 UC-60: Print Prescription** {#11.7-uc-60:-print-prescription}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to print the prescription for the patient, so that the patient can buy the medication outside the hospital (BR-33). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. A prescription has been saved for the visit (UC-59). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor clicks Print Prescription. 2\. The system builds the prescription (PF-05): hospital name, patient information (name, age, gender, address, insurance card number if any), diagnosis with ICD-10 code, drug lines (name, strength, unit, quantity, usage instructions), general note, follow-up date (if any – UC-61), Doctor (academic title \+ full name), date. 3\. The system sends the prescription to the office printer (HW-02) and shows a preview. 4\. The Doctor hands the prescription to the patient. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 1): Reprint after closing** 1\. The Doctor opens the closed visit from the medical record (UC-52) and prints; the prescription is marked "Copy". *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 3): The printer fails** 1\. The system shows MSG52. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient receives the printed prescription. No data is changed (the print is logged). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-33, BR-34 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG52 |  |  |

### **11.8 UC-61: Create Follow-up Appointment** {#11.8-uc-61:-create-follow-up-appointment}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to set a follow-up date and advice for a patient under periodic monitoring (hypertension, diabetes), so that the patient comes back on time. The follow-up date must be after the current visit date and is printed on the appointment slip and the prescription (BR-34). No SMS or phone reminder is sent. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The conclusion of the visit has been saved (UC-56) and the record is not closed. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor clicks Create Follow-up Appointment. 2\. The system shows the form: Follow-up date\*, Room (default: current room), Reason for monitoring\* (Hypertension, Diabetes, Other chronic disease), Advice / tests to prepare. 3\. The Doctor fills in the form and clicks Save. 4\. The system checks that the follow-up date is after the current visit date (BR-34) and that the required fields are filled in. 5\. The system saves the appointment linked to the visit and the patient and records it in the audit log. 6\. The system shows MSG03 and the action Print Follow-up Appointment (UC-62). The date will also be printed on the prescription (UC-60). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The diagnosis is not a chronic disease under periodic monitoring** 1\. The system shows MSG66; the Doctor may cancel or select Other chronic disease with a note. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **AF-02 (at step 3): Change the appointment before closing** 1\. The Doctor changes the date or advice and saves again. *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 4): The date is not after the visit date** 1\. The system shows MSG35. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 4): Required field empty** 1\. The system shows MSG02. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-03 (at step 5): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the follow-up appointment is saved; on the follow-up date the patient is shown to the Receptionist (background job 6\) and the reason is pre-filled at registration (UC-40, AF-04). Failure: no appointment is saved. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-32, BR-34 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG03, MSG12, MSG35, MSG66, MSG99 |  |  |

### **11.9 UC-62: Print Follow-up Appointment** {#11.9-uc-62:-print-follow-up-appointment}

| Primary Actors | Doctor | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Doctor, I want to print the follow-up appointment slip for the patient, so that the patient remembers the date of the next visit (BR-34). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. A follow-up appointment has been saved for the visit (UC-61). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Doctor clicks Print Follow-up Appointment. 2\. The system builds the slip: hospital name, patient code and name, year of birth, diagnosis, follow-up date, room and location, advice / tests to prepare, Doctor, date. 3\. The system sends the slip to the office printer (HW-02) and shows a preview. 4\. The Doctor hands the slip to the patient. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 1): Reprint after closing** 1\. The Doctor opens the closed visit from the medical record (UC-52) and prints; the slip is marked "Copy". *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 3): The printer fails** 1\. The system shows MSG52. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient receives the follow-up appointment slip. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-34 |  |  |

## **12\. Paraclinical Service** {#12.-paraclinical-service}

### **12.1 UC-63: View Waiting Paraclinical List** {#12.1-uc-63:-view-waiting-paraclinical-list}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to see the waiting list of paid (or fee-exempt) paraclinical services routed to my room, so that I know which patient to call next. Orders only reach the room after payment is confirmed or if the patient amount is 0 (BR-26), are routed to the active room with the fewest waiting patients (BR-28) and are ordered by priority first, then registration time (BR-18). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Technician is signed in and is assigned to an Active paraclinical room (UC-15). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician opens the Technician Dashboard (home screen after sign-in) or selects Paraclinical Waiting List. 2\. The system shows the room name and the tabs: Waiting (default), Skipped (UC-45), Pending Result (UC-64). 3\. The system shows the orders of this room with status Waiting: patient name, age, gender, priority mark, service, ordering Doctor and room, clinical note, released time, registration time. 4\. The system orders the list: priority patients first, then by registration time of the visit (BR-18). 5\. The system refreshes the list automatically at least every 10 seconds (UI-04). 6\. The Technician clicks Call Next or Call on an order. *\=\>Continue in UC-65.* |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 3): The list is empty** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>Continue at step 5\.* **AF-02 (at step 3): An order is In Progress by another technician of the room** 1\. The system shows it in a separate "In progress" section with the technician's name. *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The Technician is not assigned to any room** 1\. The system shows MSG50 and an empty list. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99 and keeps the last loaded list. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The Technician sees the ordered waiting list of their room. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-14, BR-18, BR-19, BR-26, BR-28; UI-04 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG50, MSG99 |  |  |

### **12.2 UC-64: View Pending Result List** {#12.2-uc-64:-view-pending-result-list}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to see the services I have performed whose results are not submitted yet, ordered by performed time, so that I do not forget to enter and submit any result. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Technician is signed in and is assigned to an Active paraclinical room. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician opens the Pending Result tab. 2\. The system shows the orders performed by this Technician (status Performed, result not submitted – BR-29): patient name, service, performed time, draft saved (Yes/No), ordering Doctor. 3\. The system orders the list by performed time, earliest first. 4\. The Technician selects an order. *\=\>Continue in UC-67.* |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The list is empty** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-02 (at step 2): Show the whole room** 1\. The Technician selects "All technicians of the room"; the list is read-only for orders performed by others (only the performer can record the result – BR-29). *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The Technician is not assigned to any room** 1\. The system shows MSG50. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The pending results of the Technician are shown. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-19, BR-29 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG50, MSG99 |  |  |

### **12.3 UC-65: Accept Paraclinical Order** {#12.3-uc-65:-accept-paraclinical-order}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to call the next paid service in my room and accept it if the patient is present, so that I can start performing it; if the patient is absent, the order moves to the skipped list (BR-20, BR-21). Only paid or fee-exempt orders can be accepted (BR-26). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Technician is viewing the waiting list of their room (UC-63) and it contains at least one order. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician clicks Call Next (first order of the list) or Call on a selected order. 2\. The system checks that the order is still Waiting, routed to this room, and that its receipt is Paid (or fee-exempt) (BR-26). 3\. The system announces the call (queue display HW-04) and marks the order "Calling". 4\. The patient comes into the room with the order slip. 5\. The Technician clicks Accept. 6\. The system sets the order to In Progress, assigns it to the Technician (performer) with the start time and records it in the audit log. 7\. The system shows the order detail (patient, service, clinical note, allergies) and the action Confirm Performed (UC-66). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 4): The patient is absent** 1\. The Technician clicks Absent. 2\. The system sets the order to Skipped, records the skip time and adds it to the room's skipped list ordered by skip time (BR-21); the system shows MSG58. *\=\>Return to step 1\.* **AF-02 (at step 4): The patient does not respond the first time** 1\. The Technician clicks Call Again. *\=\>Return to step 4\.* **AF-03 (at step 6): The patient also has orders in other rooms** 1\. The system shows the other orders and their rooms so that the Technician can tell the patient where to go next. *\=\>Continue at step 7\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): The order is not paid** 1\. The system shows MSG28 and does not accept it. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 2): The order was already called or accepted by another technician** 1\. The system shows MSG23 and refreshes the list. *\=\>Return to step 1\.* **EF-03 (at step 6): Session expired or system errorr** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; the order stays Waiting. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Present: the order is In Progress and assigned to the Technician. Absent: the order is Skipped until the patient returns (UC-46) or the day ends; at the end of the day it is cancelled and the visit becomes Abandoned (BR-22). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-18, BR-19, BR-20, BR-21, BR-22, BR-26 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG12, MSG23, MSG28, MSG58, MSG99 |  |  |

### **12.4 UC-66: Perform Paraclinical Order** {#12.4-uc-66:-perform-paraclinical-order}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to confirm that the accepted service has been performed, so that the order status is updated and the result can be entered. The service itself (ultrasound, X-ray, CT, MRI, endoscopy, ECG, laboratory tests) is performed with the equipment outside the system; results are entered manually (SW-04). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The order is In Progress and assigned to the Technician (UC-65 or UC-46). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician performs the service with the patient (with the paraclinical doctor where required, e.g. ultrasound or endoscopy teams). 2\. The Technician clicks Confirm Performed on the order. 3\. The system sets the order to Performed with the performed time and adds it to the Technician's pending result list (UC-64). 4\. The system shows MSG03 and the action Record Result (UC-67). 5\. The patient goes to the next paraclinical room if the visit has other orders, or waits for the results and then returns to the original Doctor. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The result can be entered right away (e.g. ECG)** 1\. The Technician clicks Record Result directly; the system sets the order to Performed. *\=\>Continue in UC-67.* **AF-02 (at step 1): The service cannot be performed (patient not prepared, equipment problem)** 1\. The Technician clicks Return to Waiting with a reason; the order goes back to Waiting at its original place and the reason is recorded. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): The order is not assigned to this Technician** 1\. The system shows MSG13. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 3): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; the order stays In Progress. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the order is Performed and waits for its result. Failure: the order stays In Progress. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-19, BR-29 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG03, MSG12, MSG13, MSG99 |  |  |

### **12.5 UC-67: Record Paraclinical Result** {#12.5-uc-67:-record-paraclinical-result}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | Cloudinary Upload API (result files) |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to enter, review and submit the result of a service I performed (content, conclusion, files), so that it is attached to the patient's medical record and sent to the examining Doctor. A Technician can only record results for services they performed, and a submitted result cannot be edited (BR-29). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The order is Performed (or In Progress, UC-66 AF-01) and the Technician is its performer. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician opens the order from the pending result list (UC-64). 2\. The system shows the result form: patient and service information, Result content\* (values with units and reference ranges for lab tests, description for imaging and functional tests), Result conclusion\*, Attached files (images or PDF, at most 10 files, each at most 20 MB). 3\. The Technician enters the result and uploads the files. 4\. The system uploads the files to the file storage (Cloudinary Upload API) and keeps their protected links. 5\. The Technician clicks Save draft to review, then Submit. 6\. The system checks the required fields and file types/sizes. 7\. The system shows MSG06 warning that the result cannot be edited after submission. 8\. The Technician confirms. 9\. The system saves and locks the result, sets the order to Completed, attaches the result to the medical record of the visit and records it in the audit log (BR-29). 10\. The system checks whether every order of the visit has a result; if so, the visit becomes Waiting for Conclusion, appears in the conclusion waiting list of the original room and the Doctor is notified (BR-18, BR-28; background job 8). 11\. The system shows MSG29 and the action Print Result (UC-68). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 5): Save draft only** 1\. The system saves the draft without locking it; the order stays in the pending result list. *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-02 (at step 10): Other orders of the visit are still not completed** 1\. The visit stays Waiting for Paraclinical; the Doctor sees the progress (UC-54). *\=\>Continue at step 11\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 6): Required field empty, wrong file type or file too large** 1\. The system shows MSG02 or MSG05. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 4): The upload fails** 1\. The system shows MSG99; the entered text is kept and the Technician can upload again. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-03 (at step 1): The Technician is not the performer** 1\. The form is read-only and the system shows MSG13. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-04 (at step 1): The result was already submitted** 1\. The system shows MSG61; the result is read-only. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-05 (at step 9): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; the result is not submitted. *\=\>Return to step 5\.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the result is locked and attached to the medical record; the order is Completed; when all orders are completed the visit is Waiting for Conclusion and the Doctor is notified. Failure: the result is not submitted (a draft may be saved). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-18, BR-19, BR-28, BR-29; Data rules: One result per order item, Medical data is access-controlled (I.3.3); SW-04 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG05, MSG06, MSG12, MSG13, MSG29, MSG61, MSG99 |  |  |

### **12.6 UC-68: Print Paraclinical Result** {#12.6-uc-68:-print-paraclinical-result}

| Primary Actors | Technician | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Technician, I want to print the paraclinical result for the patient, so that the patient keeps a paper copy of the result. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The result of the order has been submitted (UC-67). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Technician clicks Print Result. 2\. The system builds the result form (PF-03): hospital name, patient information, registration code, service, ordering Doctor, result content, images (if any), result conclusion, Technician (and paraclinical doctor), performed and submitted time. 3\. The system sends the form to the office printer (HW-02) and shows a preview. 4\. The Technician hands the result to the patient. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 1): Reprint** 1\. The Technician opens the completed order from the room's history and prints; the form is marked "Copy". *\=\>Continue at step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The result is not submitted yet** 1\. The Print button is disabled (drafts cannot be printed). *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 3): The printer fails** 1\. The system shows MSG52. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient receives the printed result. No data is changed (the print is logged). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-29 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG52 |  |  |

## **13\. Payment** {#13.-payment}

### **13.1 UC-69: View Waiting Payment List** {#13.1-uc-69:-view-waiting-payment-list}

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Cashier, I want to see the pending receipts created automatically by the system — examination fee receipts at registration and paraclinical receipts when a Doctor confirms an order — so that I can collect the fees of the patients at the counter. Receipts are generated by the system; the Cashier cannot create them manually (BR-36). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Cashier is signed in (UC-01). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Cashier opens the Cashier Dashboard (home screen after sign-in) or selects Waiting Payment List. 2\. The system shows the receipts with status Pending: receipt number, type (Examination fee / Paraclinical fee), registration code, patient code and name, priority mark, visit type and coverage rate, created time, total amount, insurance amount, patient amount (BR-27). 3\. The system orders the list by created time (priority patients highlighted) and refreshes it automatically (UI-04). 4\. The Cashier filters by type or searches (UC-70) for the patient at the counter. 5\. The Cashier selects a receipt. *\=\>Continue in UC-71.* |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The list is empty** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The user is not a Cashier** 1\. The system shows MSG13. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The pending receipts are shown. No data is changed. Receipts still Pending at the end of the day are cancelled by the end-of-day job (BR-22). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-15, BR-22, BR-26, BR-27, BR-36, BR-37; Permission Matrix 4.4 (Invoice) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG13, MSG99 |  |  |

### **13.2 UC-70: Search Payment** {#13.2-uc-70:-search-payment}

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Cashier, I want to search for a receipt by receipt number, patient name or code, or registration code, so that I can quickly find the receipt of the patient at the counter or answer a question about a past payment. |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Cashier is signed in (UC-01). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Cashier enters a keyword in the search box of the payment screens. 2\. The system validates the keyword (at least 2 characters). 3\. The system searches all receipts (Pending, Paid, Cancelled) by receipt number, patient code, patient name (case- and accent-insensitive) or registration code, with optional filters: status, type, date range. 4\. The system shows the matching receipts: receipt number, type, status, patient, registration code, created time, paid time, patient amount. 5\. The Cashier selects a receipt: a Pending receipt opens Confirm Payment (UC-71); a Paid receipt opens its detail with Print (UC-72); a Cancelled receipt opens read-only with the cancel reason. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 4): Exactly one Pending receipt matches the registration code** 1\. The system opens UC-71 directly. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 2): Keyword too short** 1\. The system shows MSG05. *\=\>Return to step 1\.* **EF-02 (at step 4): No receipt matches** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>Return to step 1\.* **EF-03 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The matching receipts are shown. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-36, BR-37 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG05, MSG12, MSG99 |  |  |

### **13.3 UC-71: Confirm Payment** {#13.3-uc-71:-confirm-payment}

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Cashier, I want to confirm that the patient has paid a receipt and record the payment method, so that the patient can continue: an examination fee puts the visit in the room's examination waiting list, and a paraclinical fee releases the orders and routes them to the least busy room that performs each service (BR-15, BR-26, BR-28). The software only records the Cashier's "paid" confirmation; it does not process money or accounting reconciliation (BR-36). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Cashier has selected a Pending receipt (UC-69 or UC-70). 2\. The patient is at the counter. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The system shows the receipt detail: receipt number, type, patient, registration code, visit type and coverage rate, and the lines: service, unit price, insurance amount, patient amount; totals (BR-27). Receipts never contain medication (BR-33). 2\. The Cashier tells the patient the amount to pay; the patient pays at the counter in cash or by bank transfer (outside the software). 3\. The Cashier selects the payment method\* (Cash, Bank transfer) and clicks Confirm Payment. 4\. The system checks that the receipt is still Pending. 5\. The system shows MSG06 with the amount. 6\. The Cashier confirms. 7\. The system sets the receipt to Paid with the payment method, Cashier and paid time, and records it in the audit log (BR-37). 8\. The system continues the visit according to the receipt type: – Examination fee: the visit becomes Waiting and appears in the examination waiting list of its room, ordered by priority and registration time (BR-15, BR-18); – Paraclinical fee: each order becomes Waiting and is routed to the Active room with the fewest waiting patients among the rooms that perform the service (BR-26, BR-28). 9\. The system shows MSG30 and prints the receipt (UC-72). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 2): The patient does not agree to pay now** 1\. The Cashier closes the receipt without confirming; it stays Pending. If it is not paid by the end of the day, it is cancelled and the visit becomes Abandoned (BR-22). *\=\>The use case ends.* **AF-02 (at step 8): No Active room performs a service** 1\. The order stays Waiting without a room and is routed as soon as a room of the service group is Active; the system warns the Cashier and the Admin dashboard shows the order. *\=\>Continue at step 9\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 3): No payment method selected** 1\. The system shows MSG02. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 4): The receipt is no longer Pending (already paid or cancelled)** 1\. The system shows MSG64 and reloads the receipt. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-03 (at step 7): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99; the receipt stays Pending (all or nothing). *\=\>Return to step 3\.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | Success: the receipt is Paid and cannot be edited or deleted; the patient joins the room's examination waiting list (examination fee) or the orders are in the waiting lists of the paraclinical rooms (paraclinical fee). Failure / Cancelled: the receipt stays Pending. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-15, BR-18, BR-22, BR-26, BR-27, BR-28, BR-33, BR-36, BR-37; Data rule: Paid payments are permanent (I.3.3) |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG02, MSG06, MSG12, MSG30, MSG64, MSG99 |  |  |

### **13.4 UC-72: Print Payment Receipt** {#13.4-uc-72:-print-payment-receipt}

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Cashier, I want to print the receipt for the patient after the payment is confirmed, so that the patient has proof of payment and, for paraclinical fees, knows the rooms to go to. Receipts are issued and printed by the Cashier at the counter and can only be printed after payment is confirmed (BR-36, BR-37). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The receipt is Paid (UC-71). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Cashier clicks Print Receipt (or the system opens the print preview after UC-71). 2\. The system builds the receipt (PF-06): hospital name, receipt number, patient code and name, registration code, visit type and coverage rate, lines with service, unit price, insurance amount and patient amount, totals, payment method, Cashier, paid time. 3\. For a paraclinical receipt, the system adds the assigned room and location of each service (BR-28); for an examination fee receipt, the room and queue number of the visit. 4\. The system sends the receipt to the printer and shows a preview. 5\. The Cashier hands the receipt to the patient. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 1): Reprint (from UC-70 or UC-73)** 1\. The Cashier opens a Paid receipt and clicks Print; the receipt is marked "Copy" and the reprint is logged. *\=\>Continue at step 4\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 1): The receipt is not Paid** 1\. The Print button is disabled and the system shows MSG62. *\=\>The use case ends.* **EF-02 (at step 4): The printer fails** 1\. The system shows MSG52; the payment is not affected. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The patient receives the printed receipt. No data is changed (the print is logged). |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-27, BR-28, BR-33, BR-36, BR-37 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG52, MSG62 |  |  |

### **13.5 UC-73: View Payment History** {#13.5-uc-73:-view-payment-history}

| Primary Actors | Cashier | Secondary Actors | None |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Description** | As a Cashier, I want to view the history of receipts that have been paid or cancelled, so that I can check what I collected during my shift and answer patients' questions. Paid receipts cannot be changed (BR-37). |  |  |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Cashier is signed in (UC-01). |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | 1\. The Cashier selects Payment History. 2\. The system shows the filters: Date range (default: today), Status (Paid, Cancelled), Type (Examination fee, Paraclinical fee), Payment method, Cashier (default: me). 3\. The Cashier selects the filters and clicks View. 4\. The system shows the receipts: receipt number, type, status, patient, registration code, paid or cancelled time, payment method, Cashier, patient amount, insurance amount; plus totals of the patient amount per payment method. 5\. The Cashier selects a receipt. 6\. The system shows its detail (lines, amounts, cancel reason for Cancelled receipts) and the Print action for Paid receipts (UC-72). |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows** | **AF-01 (at step 4): Sort by time or amount** 1\. The system sorts the list. *\=\>Return to step 4\.* |  |  |
| **Exception Flows** | **EF-01 (at step 3): Invalid date range** 1\. The system shows MSG53. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-02 (at step 4): No receipt matches** 1\. The system shows MSG01. *\=\>Return to step 3\.* **EF-03 (any step): Session expired or system error** 1\. The system shows MSG12 or MSG99. *\=\>The use case ends.* |  |  |
| **Postconditions** | The payment history is shown. No data is changed. |  |  |
| **Business Rules** | BR-22, BR-36, BR-37 |  |  |
| **Messages** | MSG01, MSG12, MSG53, MSG99 |  |  |

# **III. Functional Requirements** {#iii.-functional-requirements}

## **1\. Authentication & Profile** {#1.-authentication-&-profile-1}

### **1.1: Login** {#1.1:-login}

![][image15]

This screen allows staff to: 

* Log in to the system to perform assigned tasks.. 

**Field Description**

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Tên đăng nhập | Tên đăng nhập của nhân viên trong hệ thống. Không phân biệt chữ hoa/thường; khoảng trắng đầu/cuối được tự động loại bỏ. Bắt buộc nhập. Tối đa 100 ký tự.  |
| Mật khẩu | Mật khẩu tương ứng với tài khoản. Hiển thị dưới dạng ký tự ẩn; có nút "Hiện/Ẩn" để chuyển đổi. Bắt buộc nhập. Tối đa 200 ký tự.  |

### **1.2: Change Password** {#1.2:-change-password}

![][image16]

This screen allows staff to: 

* Change their own account password to protect account security. 

**Field Description**

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Mật khẩu hiện tại | The staff member's current password. Used to verify identity before allowing the change. Input is masked; a Show/Hide toggle is available. Required. |
| Mật khẩu mới | The desired new password. Must be 8–64 Unicode characters and at most 72 UTF-8 bytes, and must differ from the current password. A live character/byte counter is displayed. Input is masked; a Show/Hide toggle is available. Required. |
| Nhập lại mật khẩu mới | Re-entry of the new password for confirmation. Must match the New Password field exactly. Validated on the client side only. Input is masked; a Show/Hide toggle is available. Required. |

### **1.3: Update Profile** {#1.3:-update-profile}

![][image17]

This screen allows staff to:

* View their account information and update their own contact details (phone number and email).

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Họ và tên | Staff member's full name. Read-only; contact an administrator to update. |
| Tên đăng nhập | The account username. Read-only; cannot be changed. |
| Giới tính | Staff member's gender. Read-only; contact an administrator to update. |
| Ngày sinh | Staff member's date of birth. Read-only; contact an administrator to update. |
| Số điện thoại | Staff member's contact phone number. Editable by the staff member. |
| Email | Staff member's contact email address. Editable by the staff member. |
| Học hàm / học vị | Academic title or degree (e.g., ThS, BS). Read-only; contact an administrator to update. |
| Số giấy phép hành nghề | Professional practice license number. Read-only; contact an administrator to update. |
| Địa chỉ | Staff member's residential address. Read-only; contact an administrator to update. |
| Vai trò | The role assigned to the staff account (e.g., Admin, Doctor, Receptionist, Cashier). Read-only. |
| Trạng thái | Current account status (e.g., Active / Inactive). Read-only. |
| Ngày tạo tài khoản | The date the account was created in the system. Read-only. |
| Đăng nhập gần nhất | Timestamp of the most recent successful login. Read-only. |
| Mật khẩu | Displays the date of the last password change, or "Chưa đổi lần nào" if never changed. Clicking **Đổi mật khẩu** navigates to the Change Password screen (1.2). |

## **2\. Account Management** {#2.-account-management-1}

### **2.1: View Account List** {#2.1:-view-account-list}

![][image18]

This screen allows the administrator to:

* View the full list of staff accounts in the system.  
* Search and filter accounts by keyword, role, department, and status.  
* Navigate to an account's detail page by clicking on a row.

**Filter / Search Fields** 

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Tìm kiếm | Free-text search box. Matches against username, full name, phone number, or email. Results update automatically with a short debounce delay. |
| Vai trò | Dropdown filter. Options: Tất cả / Admin / Doctor / Receptionist / Cashier / Technician. |
| Khoa / Phòng | Dropdown filter. Lists all active departments. Filters accounts assigned to the selected department. |
| Trạng thái | Dropdown filter. Options: Tất cả / Đang hoạt động / Bị khóa. |

**Table Columns** 

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| STT | Sequential row number within the current page. |
| Tên đăng nhập | The account's unique username. Sortable. |
| Họ và tên | Staff member's full name, displayed with avatar initials and academic title if available. Sortable. |
| Vai trò | The role assigned to the account (e.g., Admin, Doctor, Receptionist). Sortable. |
| Khoa / Phòng | The department and examination/lab room the account is assigned to. Displays "—" if not assigned. |
| Email | Staff member's email address. |
| Số điện thoại | Staff member's contact phone number. |
| Đăng nhập cuối | Date and time of the most recent successful login. Displays "Chưa đăng nhập" if the account has never logged in. Sortable. |
| Trạng thái | Current account status badge: **Đang hoạt động** or **Bị khóa**. An additional **Chờ đổi mật khẩu** badge is shown when the account has a temporary password that has not yet been changed. Sortable. |

**Other Controls** 

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Xóa bộ lọc | Resets all filters and search to their default state. |
| Tạo tài khoản | Navigates to the Create Account screen (2.2). |
| Số dòng / trang | Dropdown to select how many rows are shown per page. |
| Phân trang | Pagination controls to navigate between pages. Displays current range and total count (e.g., "Hiển thị 1–5 / 5 tài khoản"). |

### **2.2: View Account Detail** {#2.2:-view-account-detail}

![][image19]

This screen allows the administrator to:

* View full information, account status, and access permissions of a staff account.  
* Access management actions: edit, change role, assign room, reset password, lock/unlock account.

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Mã tài khoản | Unique system-generated account ID (UUID). Read-only. |
| Họ và tên | Staff member's full name. |
| Học hàm / học vị | Academic title or degree (e.g., ThS, BS). Displays "—" if not set. |
| Số giấy phép hành nghề | Professional practice license number. Displays "—" if not set. |
| Tên đăng nhập | The account's unique username. |
| Ngày sinh | Date of birth with calculated age in parentheses. Displays "—" if not set. |
| Giới tính | Gender (Nam / Nữ / Khác). Displays "—" if not set. |
| Số điện thoại | Contact phone number. Displays "—" if not set. |
| Email | Contact email address. Displays "—" if not set. |
| Địa chỉ | Residential address. Displays "—" if not set. |
| Phòng làm việc | The examination or lab room assigned to the account. Displays "Chưa được phân công" if unassigned; "Không áp dụng cho vai trò này" for roles that do not require a room. |
| Vai trò | The role assigned to the account (e.g., Admin, Doctor, Receptionist, Cashier, Technician). |
| Phân hệ truy cập | List of system modules the role has access to. |
| Đổi mật khẩu lần cuối | Date of the last password change and how many days ago. Displays "Chưa đổi" if never changed. |
| Yêu cầu đổi mật khẩu | Whether the account must change its password on next login (Có / Không). |
| Đăng nhập sai liên tiếp | Number of consecutive failed login attempts since the last successful login. |
| Chặn đăng nhập đến | Datetime until which login is temporarily blocked after 5 consecutive failures. Displays "Không bị chặn" if not currently blocked. |
| Trạng thái khóa | Whether the account is administratively locked (Đang khóa / Không khóa). |
| Lượt khám đang xử lý | Number of active patient visits currently assigned to this account. |
| Chỉ định CLS đang xử lý | Number of active paraclinical orders currently assigned to this account. |
| Tóm tắt quyền hạn | List of individual permission actions granted to the account's role. |
| Lịch sử đăng nhập | Chronological log of login events (successful login, logout, failed login, throttled), including timestamp and IP address. Paginated (5 per page). |
| Lịch sử thay đổi tài khoản | Audit trail of administrative changes (e.g., role change, profile update, password reset), showing actor, timestamp, and before/after field values. Paginated (5 per page). |

### **2.3: Create Account** {#2.3:-create-account}

![][image20]

This screen allows the administrator to:

* Create a new staff account and assign an initial role and password.

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Họ và tên | Staff member's full name. Required. |
| Tên đăng nhập | Unique username for the account. Must be 4–30 characters; only lowercase letters (a–z), digits (0–9), dots, and underscores are allowed. Automatically converted to lowercase. Required. |
| Giới tính | Staff member's gender (Nam / Nữ / Khác). Optional. |
| Ngày sinh | Staff member's date of birth. Optional. |
| Số điện thoại | Contact phone number. Must be exactly 10 digits starting with 0\. Required. |
| Email | Contact email address. Must be unique across all accounts including locked ones. Optional. |
| Học hàm / học vị | Academic title or degree (e.g., BSCKI, ThS.BS). Optional for most roles; required for Doctor and Technician. |
| Số giấy phép hành nghề | Professional practice license number. Required for Doctor and Technician roles; optional for others. |
| Địa chỉ | Residential address. Maximum 255 characters. Optional. |
| Vai trò | The role to assign to the account. Options: Doctor, Receptionist, Cashier, Technician. Admin role cannot be assigned via this form. Required. |
| Phân hệ được truy cập | Read-only display of the system modules accessible by the selected role. Updates automatically when the role changes. |
| Mật khẩu *(chế độ Hệ thống tự sinh)* | The system generates a random 12-character temporary password. The account is required to change it on first login. |
| Mật khẩu *(chế độ Admin nhập thủ công)* | Admin sets an official password directly. Must be 8–64 Unicode characters and at most 72 UTF-8 bytes. The account is not required to change it on first login. |
| Xác nhận mật khẩu | Re-entry of the manually entered password. Must match exactly. Visible only when "Admin nhập thủ công" mode is selected. |
| Trạng thái ban đầu | Fixed as **Hoạt động** (Active). All newly created accounts are active by default. Read-only. |
| Lần đăng nhập đầu | Displays whether the account must change its password on first login, based on the selected password mode. Read-only. |

### **2.4: Update Account Information** {#2.4:-update-account-information}

![][image21]

This screen allows the administrator to:

* Edit a staff account's personal and contact information.  
* Lock or unlock the account directly from the edit form.

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Tên đăng nhập | The account's username. Read-only; cannot be changed via this form. |
| Trạng thái | Current account status (Đang hoạt động / Bị khóa). Read-only; change via the Lock/Unlock control on the right panel. |
| Họ và tên | Staff member's full name. Required. |
| Giới tính | Staff member's gender (Nam / Nữ / Khác). Optional. |
| Ngày sinh | Staff member's date of birth. Optional. |
| Số điện thoại | Contact phone number. Must be exactly 10 digits starting with 0\. Required. |
| Email | Contact email address. Must be unique across all accounts. Optional. |
| Học hàm / học vị | Academic title or degree (e.g., BSCKI, ThS.BS). Optional. |
| Số giấy phép hành nghề | Professional practice license number. Required for Doctor and Technician roles; optional for others. |
| Địa chỉ | Residential address. Maximum 255 characters. Optional. |

### **2.5: Assign Role** {#2.5:-assign-role}

![][image22]

This screen allows the administrator to:

* Change the role assigned to a staff account and preview the permissions that come with the new role before applying.

| Field Name | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Vai trò hiện tại | The role currently assigned to the account. Read-only; displayed in the account summary panel. |
| Ngày tạo | The date the account was created. Read-only. |
| Đăng nhập gần nhất | Timestamp of the most recent successful login. Displays "Chưa đăng nhập" if never logged in. Read-only. |

| Phân hệ | Number of system modules accessible by the current role. Read-only. |

### **2.6: Lock/Unlock Account** {#2.6:-lock/unlock-account}

![][image23]

This screen allows the administrator to:

| Khoa | Disabled text field. Displays the department of the room. Staff assigned to this room belong to this department (BR-05). Cannot be modified. |
| Loại phòng | Disabled text field. Displays the room type: Lâm sàng or Cận lâm sàng. The type determines the assignable role: Doctor for a clinical room, Technician for a paraclinical room. Cannot be modified. |
| Vị trí | Disabled text field. Displays the room location. Cannot be modified. |
| Trạng thái | Disabled text field. Displays the room status. This screen is available only for an active room (Đang hoạt động). Cannot be modified. |
| Nhân viên đang được phân công (n) | Table of staff currently assigned to the room. n is the number of staff in the table. If the table has no data, the system shows MSG92. |
| Họ tên | Read-only text. Displays the title and full name of the assigned staff member. |
| Số GPHN | Read-only text. Displays the practice licence number of the assigned staff member. |
| Gỡ khỏi phòng | Button on each row. Disabled if the staff member has a shift from today onwards or work in progress (BR-55, BR-113). |
| Tìm kiếm | Optional, maximum 100 characters, case- and accent-insensitive, leading and trailing spaces are trimmed (BR-110). Filters the table by full name or practice licence number as the Admin types. If nothing matches, the system shows MSG01.  |
| Nhân viên có thể phân công (n) | Table of active staff whose role matches the room type. n is the number of staff in the table. If the table has no data, the system shows MSG92. |
| Chọn | Checkbox on each row to select staff. Disabled for staff with a shift from today onwards or work in progress (BR-55, BR-113). |
| Họ tên (Số GPHN) | Read-only text. Displays the title and full name of the staff member, with the practice licence number in brackets. |
| Phòng hiện tại | Read-only text. Displays the current room (code and name) of the staff member, or “Chưa có phòng” if none. |
| Thêm (n) | Button. n is the number of selected staff. Disabled when no staff is selected.  |
| Đóng | Button. Closes the screen and returns to the previous screen. |

## **14\. Background Job Inventory** {#14.-background-job-inventory}

### **14.1 Unlock Expired Locked Accounts (JOB-01)** {#14.1-unlock-expired-locked-accounts-(job-01)}

***Trigger***: Scheduled — every 15 minutes

***Purpose***: Automatically unlocks accounts that were locked after failed sign-in attempts, once the lockout duration has elapsed

***Processing steps*****:**

1. Find all accounts with status \= Locked where the lockout timestamp is more than 10 minutes ago.  
2. For each account found: reset the failed sign-in count to zero, set status back to Active.  
3. Log the number of accounts unlocked in this run.

***Failure behavior*****:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| ----- | ----- |
| Database unreachable | Job retries up to 3 times with 30-second intervals. If still failing, logs a critical error. Accounts remain locked until the next successful run. |
| No locked accounts found | Job completes immediately with no action — this is normal and expected. |

### **14.2 Clean Up Old Audit Log Entries (JOB-02)** {#14.2-clean-up-old-audit-log-entries-(job-02)}

***Trigger***: Scheduled — daily at 2:00 AM

***Purpose***: Removes audit log entries older than the configured retention period to prevent unbounded database growth.

***Processing steps:***

1. Determine the configured log retention period (default: 90 days).  
2. Find all audit log entries with a timestamp older than the retention threshold.  
3. Delete the old entries in batches of up to 5,000 records per run — to avoid locking the database for an extended period.  
4. If records remain after one batch, schedule the next batch to run 5 minutes later rather than deleting everything at once.  
5. Log the total number of entries deleted and the number of batches processed.

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| ----- | ----- |
| Database timeout during delete | Current batch rolled back. Job logs a warning. Tries again at the next scheduled time. No data corruption. |
| Retention period not configured | Job uses default of 90 days and logs a warning that the setting was not found. |

### **15.3 SePay Webhook (API-03)** {#15.3-sepay-webhook-(api-03)}

| *URL* | POST: /api/v1/commerce/payment/webhook/sepay |
| :---- | :---- |
| ***Purpose*** | Receives payment confirmation from SePay; triggers access grant creation |
| ***Caller*** | SePay payment gateway |
| ***Auth*** | HMAC signature validation |
