# **IV. Non-Functional Requirements** {#iv.-non-functional-requirements}

## **1\. External Interfaces** {#1.-external-interfaces}

### **1.1 User Interfaces** {#1.1-user-interfaces}

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| UI-01 | The system is a web application. All screens are in Vietnamese; dates use the format dd/MM/yyyy, time uses 24-hour format (HH:mm), and money is shown in VND with thousand separators (e.g. 150.000 ₫). |
| UI-02 | After signing in, each user lands on the dashboard of their role: Admin \=\>Admin Dashboard; Receptionist \=\>Receptionist Dashboard (today's registrations and queues); Doctor \=\>Doctor Dashboard (waiting list of the doctor's department); Technician \=\>Technician Dashboard (paid services waiting in the technician's department); Cashier \=\>Cashier Dashboard (pending payments). |
| UI-03 | Every screen shares the same layout: header (hospital name, current user, role, assigned department, sign-out), left menu containing only the functions allowed for the role (see 4.4 Permission Matrix), and main content area. |
| UI-04 | Waiting lists (clinical departments, paraclinical departments, pending payments) refresh automatically at least every 10 seconds without reloading the page. Priority patients are highlighted and shown first (BR-18). |
| UI-05 | Statuses are shown with the same color code on all screens: registration – WAITING, IN\_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELLED, ABANDONED; payment – PENDING, PAID, CANCELLED; paraclinical service – PENDING\_PAYMENT, PAID, IN\_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, EXPIRED. |
| UI-06 | Required fields are marked with (\*). Validation errors are shown in red directly under the field (MSG02, MSG08); success messages are shown as toast messages. |
| UI-07 | Irreversible actions (Conclude Examination, Cancel Registration, Confirm Payment, Cancel Payment, Lock Account, Reset Password) require a confirmation dialog (MSG06) before being executed. |
| UI-08 | Screens are optimized for desktop resolution 1366×768 and above. Main reception and examination screens must be fully usable with the keyboard (Tab / Enter / shortcut keys) to support fast data entry at peak hours. |

 

### **1.2 Hardware Interfaces** {#1.2-hardware-interfaces}

| ID | Device | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| HW-01 | Ticket printer (thermal, 80 mm) | Used at the reception desk to print examination tickets (registration code, queue number, department and location, doctor, patient name, visit type, patient amount of the exam fee, time). |
| HW-02 | Office printer (A4/A5) | Used to print paraclinical orders, paraclinical results, examination conclusions, prescriptions, follow-up appointments, invoices and medical records. Print layouts follow the forms required by the Ministry of Health where applicable. |
| HW-03 | Barcode / QR scanner (optional) | Used at reception to read the QR code on the chip-based Citizen ID card (CCCD) or health insurance card to fill in patient identification fields automatically. Manual input must always remain possible. |
| HW-04 | Queue display screen (optional) | A TV/monitor in front of each clinical or paraclinical department displays the queue number currently being called and the next numbers. |
| HW-05 | Workstations | Standard PCs with a modern web browser; no software installation is required on client machines. |

 

### **1.3 Software Interfaces** {#1.3-software-interfaces}

| ID | External system | Direction | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| SW-01 | Health Insurance Portal (Vietnam Social Security – BHXH), **simulated** | METP \=\>Portal | During reception (UC-35), the system sends the insurance card number, full name and date of birth and receives the card status, validity period, benefit code and registered primary care facility; the coverage rate is calculated from the benefit code (BR-27; Data rule: Payment calculation, I.3.3). In this project the portal is a mock service returning predefined data; the interface is designed so that it can be replaced by the real portal later. |
| SW-02 | Web browser | — | Latest two versions of Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge and Mozilla Firefox. |
| SW-03 | Export | METP \=\>File | Statistics reports are exported to Excel (.xlsx) and PDF; medical records, conclusions, prescriptions and invoices are exported to PDF for printing. |
| SW-04 | Paraclinical equipment / existing lab software | — | Direct integration with laboratory and imaging equipment is out of scope (LI-08). Technicians enter the result content and conclusion on the Update Result screen and upload result files (images, PDF), which are stored through the Cloudinary Upload API (5.2, API 1). Integration with the current paraclinical software is an open issue (Q-04). |

 

### **1.4 Communication Interfaces** {#1.4-communication-interfaces}

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| CI-01 | All communication between browser and server uses HTTPS (TLS 1.2 or higher). |
| CI-02 | Client workstations use the hospital internal network (LAN). The server also needs Internet access for the simulated insurance portal and the file storage service (Cloudinary). Access by staff from outside the hospital is not required in this version. |
| CI-03 | Calls to the (simulated) health insurance portal use HTTPS REST/JSON with a timeout of 10 seconds. If the portal does not respond, the Receptionist is informed (MSG20) and may retry or register the visit as self-paid. |
| CI-04 | Waiting list updates are pushed to clients in near real-time (WebSocket/Server-Sent Events) or by polling at most every 10 seconds. |

 

## **2\. Quality Attributes** {#2.-quality-attributes}

### **2.1 Usability**  {#2.1-usability}

### 

| ID | Requirement | Measure |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| US-01 | Training time | A new Receptionist, Doctor, Technician or Cashier can perform the main tasks of their role on their own after at most 2 hours of training. An Admin needs at most 4 hours. |
| US-02 | Registering a returning patient | Search the patient \+ register the visit \+ assign the department \+ print the ticket in at most 60 seconds and at most 6 clicks/key confirmations (excluding insurance verification time). Needed for the 7:00–9:00 peak hours. |
| US-03 | Registering a new patient | Create the patient profile and register the visit in at most 3 minutes. |
| US-04 | Calling the next patient | The Doctor/Technician calls the next patient with one click from the waiting list. |
| US-05 | Data re-use | Patient administrative data, drug allergy history and previous diagnoses are shown automatically and never need to be re-entered at later steps of the visit or at later visits. |
| US-06 | Search | Patient search accepts partial name, phone number, citizen ID or health insurance number, is accent-insensitive for Vietnamese (e.g. "nguyen" matches "Nguyễn") and shows results while typing. |
| US-07 | Error prevention | Pick lists are used instead of free text wherever possible (departments, services, ICD-10 diagnoses, drugs, units, common reasons for visit). |
| US-08 | Consistency | The same action has the same name, icon and position on every screen. |

### 

### **2.2 Performance** {#2.2-performance}

### 

| Requirement | Target | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Page load time | Any page loads within 2 seconds | Up to 100 users active simultaneously |
| Form submission response | System acknowledges within 2 seconds | Up to 100 users active simultaneously |
| Patient search | Results returned within 1 second | Database of up to 500,000 patient profiles |
| Waiting list update | A registration whose exam fee is paid, a transferred patient or a newly paid CLS service appears in the target department's list within 5 seconds | Normal operation |
| CLS result availability | A recorded CLS result is visible to the ordering Doctor within 5 seconds | Normal operation |
| Health insurance verification | Result returned within 5 seconds (excluding portal outage) | Simulated portal |
| Printing | Examination ticket is sent to the printer within 3 seconds after the registration is confirmed | Normal operation |
| Throughput at peak hours | Handles at least 300 visit registrations per hour | 7:00–9:00 peak hours |
| Report generation | Statistics for a period of up to 12 months are shown/exported within 10 seconds | Up to 1 year of visit data |
| Maximum simultaneous users | System remains fully functional for up to 100 users | Single server deployment |

### 

### **2.3 Security** {#2.3-security}

| Requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Authentication required | Every page and action other than the sign-in page requires the user to be signed in. There is no self-registration; accounts are created only by the Admin. |
| Role-based access | Each user can only see and perform the functions of their role and within the restricted scope defined in the Permission Matrix (4.4). Access rights are checked by the system on every request, not only by hiding menu items. |
| Password protection | Passwords must never be stored in a form that a person or program can read. Passwords must have 8 to 64 characters and at most 72 bytes (UTF-8). |
| Account lockout | After 5 consecutive failed sign-in or current-password attempts, password sign-in is blocked for 15 minutes. The block ends automatically when the period expires, or earlier when the Admin resets the password (UC-11). This temporary block does not change the account status; manual Lock/Unlock (UC-10) is separate and does not clear it.  |
| Session timeout | A session with no activity for 30 minutes is ended automatically and the user must sign in again. |
| Medical data confidentiality | Patient health data is sensitive personal data. Doctors can view and export the medical records of all patients, including the examination history and paraclinical results of all visits (BR-35), but can only edit the current, uncompleted visit served in their assigned room (BR-19, BR-32). Technicians only see the patients and orders routed to their room; the Cashier only sees billing information; the Receptionist only sees administrative information. Result files are never accessible through a guessable or public link, and every access to a medical record is recorded in the audit log (Data rule: Medical data is access-controlled, I.3.3). |
| Audit trail | The system records who did what and when for: sign-in/sign-out, creating/updating patient profiles, registering and cancelling visits, recording examination data, paraclinical results, diagnoses, prescriptions, concluding examinations, creating/confirming/cancelling payments, price and service changes, and all account, role and department changes. Audit entries cannot be edited or deleted by any user. |
| Closed record protection | A concluded examination (diagnosis, results, prescription) cannot be edited by anyone (BR-32). |
| No data deletion | Accounts, departments, services, patient profiles, registrations, examinations and payments are never permanently deleted; they can only be deactivated, cancelled or abandoned (Data rule: Records are never permanently deleted, I.3.3). |
| Secure transmission | All data is transmitted over HTTPS. |

# **V. Requirement Appendix** {#v.-requirement-appendix}

## **1\. Business Rules** {#1.-business-rules}

| BR-ID | Business Rule | Description | Related UCs |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-01 | Login Credentials | Usernames are unique and case-insensitive. Staff sign in with username and password. An account with status LOCKED cannot sign in. For an existing account, after 5 consecutive wrong passwords, the system temporarily blocks password sign-in for 15 minutes; this temporary block does not change the account status to LOCKED. A successful sign-in resets the failed-attempt count. A session expires after 2 hours without being refreshed and always ends at most 12 hours after sign-in. | UC-01, UC-07, UC-10 |
| BR-02 | Role-based Access | Each account has exactly one role (Admin, Receptionist, Doctor, Technician, Cashier) and can only access the functions of that role. Each staff member uses their own account; accounts are not shared. | UC-01, UC-09 |
| BR-03 | Password Change | Passwords are 8 to 64 characters long. Changing a password requires the correct current password, and the new password must differ from the old one. When a user forgets the password, only Admin can reset it; the user must change the password at the next sign-in. | UC-03, UC-11 |
| BR-04 | Profile Edit Scope | Staff can only update their own phone number and email. Other information (full name, academic title, role) can only be updated by Admin. | UC-04, UC-08, UC-09 |
| BR-05 | Staff Department | A staff member’s department is determined by their assigned room. A room can have multiple assigned staff. | UC-15 |
| BR-06 | Room Creation | Room codes are unique. A paraclinical room must specify the service group it performs. | UC-17 |
| BR-07 | Room Deactivation | A room with waiting or in-progress patients cannot be deactivated. A deactivated room cannot receive registrations, transfers or service assignments. | UC-19, UC-40, UC-48, UC-71 |
| BR-08 | Service Pricing | Each service has a clinic price. A service covered by health insurance also has an insurance price; a service without an insurance price is not covered by insurance. | UC-20, UC-22 |
| BR-09 | Price Effectiveness | A new price only applies to receipts and orders created after the update. Existing receipts and orders keep the price at the time they were created. | UC-24, UC-49 |
| BR-10 | Active Services Only | Deactivated services are hidden from the order list; the Doctor can only order active services. | UC-25, UC-49 |
| BR-11 | Visit Classification | Whether a visit is insurance or self-paid is decided at reception by the Receptionist. | UC-40 |
| BR-12 | Patient Identification | First-time and returning patients follow the same process; the only difference is whether a new profile is created. A patient profile requires a personal identification number/citizen ID (passport for foreigners), and each number maps to exactly one profile. | UC-35, UC-37, UC-38 |
| BR-13 | Insurance Verification | An insurance visit requires card verification via the simulated insurance portal, which returns the card validity and coverage rate. If the card is invalid, the visit is registered as self-paid and the Receptionist informs the patient. | UC-74, UC-40 |
| BR-14 | Priority Patient | Patients eligible for priority under the regulations are registered as priority, skip the reception counter queue, and are placed at the top of the waiting list in both examination and paraclinical rooms. | UC-40, UC-43, UC-63 |
| BR-15 | Examination Fee | An examination fee receipt is created for every visit at registration. For a self-paid visit, the examination fee is collected at the cashier counter before the patient joins the examination waiting list. For an insurance visit, the patient joins the examination waiting list immediately without paying; the examination fee and all paraclinical fees of the visit (BR-26) stay Pending and are collected once at the cashier counter after the Doctor concludes. If the total patient-payable amount is 0, the receipts automatically become Exempt. | UC-40, UC-41, UC-69, UC-71 |
| BR-16 | Examination Ticket | The examination ticket shows the visit code, queue number, examination room and room location. For a self-paid visit, it also shows the examination fee to pay at the cashier before joining the examination waiting list (BR-15). | UC-41 |
| BR-17 | Single Active Visit | A patient can only have one active visit (not yet Completed or Abandoned) at a time. | UC-40 |
| BR-18 | Waiting Lists | Each examination room has two lists: the examination waiting list (insurance visits, and self-paid visits whose examination fee is paid) and the conclusion waiting list (visits whose non-cancelled paraclinical orders all have results, or whose patient refused paraclinical services under BR-41). Queue numbers are issued in ascending order per room; a transferred visit (BR-24, BR-40) gets the next queue number of the new room and is marked “transferred”. The examination waiting list orders priority patients first, then transferred patients by transfer time (by queue number when the times are equal), then the remaining patients by queue number. All other waiting lists, including paraclinical ones, order priority patients first, then by queue number. | UC-43, UC-54, UC-63 |
| BR-19 | Room Scope | Doctors and Technicians can only view, call and handle patients or services of their assigned room. | UC-43 – UC-46, UC-54, UC-63, UC-65 |
| BR-20 | Patient Call | If the called patient is present, the visit or service continues at its current step: the examination starts and is assigned to the caller, the visit proceeds to conclusion, or the paraclinical service starts. If absent, the patient moves to the skipped list (BR-21). | UC-44, UC-46, UC-65 |
| BR-21 | Skip Mechanism | Skipping applies when calling patients for examination, for paraclinical services and for conclusion. “Skipped” is a separate status of the visit or order. The patient stays in the skipped list, ordered by skip time, until they return or the day ends. The system does not auto-recall and there is no recall limit. When the patient returns, the Doctor/Technician presses “Accept” on their name. There is no manual “Abandoned” action. | UC-44, UC-45, UC-46, UC-65 |
| BR-22 | End-of-day Job | At the end of each day, for every visit not yet “Completed” (waiting, skipped, in examination, waiting for paraclinical results or waiting for conclusion): the visit becomes “Abandoned”, with no conclusion; paraclinical orders without results become “Abandoned”; unpaid receipts become “Cancelled”. Unpaid receipts of a “Completed” visit (insurance visits pay after conclusion) stay “Pending” until the patient pays. This rule covers patients who leave without notice. | UC-43, UC-45, UC-46, UC-54, UC-69, UC-71 |
| BR-23 | Medical History & Allergies | Drug allergy is stored as a separate field in the patient profile. Medical history and allergies are only updated by the Doctor during examination; the Receptionist only updates administrative information. | UC-38, UC-39 |
| BR-24 | Patient Transfer | The Doctor can transfer a patient who is waiting, or who has been called in but whose medical record has not been opened, to another active examination room. A reason must be entered. The existing visit is reused and returns to “Waiting for Examination” in the new room with that room’s next queue number, marked “transferred” so it is called before regular patients (BR-18). The system shows the new queue number and allows the examination ticket to be reprinted; no additional examination fee is charged. | UC-48 |
| BR-25 | Paraclinical Order | The Doctor orders all paraclinical services they consider necessary; confirming the order creates the paraclinical receipt. The Doctor then explains the services and estimated cost to the patient. If the patient refuses, the Doctor cancels each refused service with a mandatory reason (BR-41), and the receipt is recalculated. A service can only be cancelled if it is unpaid (self-paid visit) or not yet accepted by a Technician (insurance visit). Otherwise, an order that has not been performed is only closed by the end-of-day job (BR-22). | UC-49 |
| BR-26 | Paraclinical Payment & Release | A paraclinical receipt is created when the Doctor confirms the order, for every visit. For a self-paid visit, the order only reaches the paraclinical room after the Cashier confirms payment. For an insurance visit, the order is released to the paraclinical room immediately; the patient-payable amount (BR-27) is collected together with the examination fee after the Doctor concludes (BR-15). | UC-49, UC-63, UC-69, UC-71 |
| BR-27 | Receipt Breakdown | Every receipt (examination fee, paraclinical fee) separates, on each service line, the insurance-covered amount from the patient-payable amount. For an insurance visit with a valid card, a service with an insurance price (BR-08) is calculated as follows: insurance-covered amount \= min(insurance price, clinic price) × the card’s coverage rate; patient-payable amount \= clinic price − insurance-covered amount, which includes the co-payment and the difference between the clinic price and the insurance price. Services without an insurance price, and all services of a self-paid visit, are charged at the clinic price and paid in full by the patient. | UC-31, UC-40, UC-49, UC-71 |
| BR-28 | Paraclinical Routing | When an order is released (BR-26), the system automatically assigns each service to the active room with the fewest waiting services among the rooms that perform it; on a tie, the room with the lower code is chosen. A visit can have multiple orders in multiple rooms. Once every non-cancelled order of the visit has a result, the visit moves to the conclusion waiting list of the examination room that ordered it. | UC-71, UC-54 |
| BR-29 | Result Submission | A Technician can only record results for services they performed. A submitted result is locked and cannot be edited; the system records the submitter and the submission time. | UC-64, UC-67 |
| BR-30 | Conclusion Prerequisite | The Doctor can only conclude when every non-cancelled paraclinical order of the visit has a result. | UC-54, UC-56 |
| BR-31 | Diagnosis Coding | The final diagnosis must have exactly one ICD-10 main diagnosis code and zero or more secondary diagnosis codes, chosen from the diagnosis catalog. The initial diagnosis at examination also uses codes from the same catalog. Each diagnosis stores the code and disease name at the time it is recorded; catalog updates do not change saved diagnoses. | UC-32, UC-47, UC-56 |
| BR-32 | Visit Closure | When the Doctor confirms the conclusion (with the prescription and follow-up appointment, if any), the system automatically closes the record and moves the visit to “Completed” in the same action. A closed record is locked and cannot be edited. The prescription (BR-33) and follow-up appointment (BR-34) must be completed before the conclusion is confirmed. | UC-58 |
| BR-33 | Prescription | The clinic does not sell or dispense medication; receipts never include drug costs. The Doctor prescribes in the system from the active medicine catalog. Each prescription has a unique prescription number and is printed for the patient. | UC-59, UC-60 |
| BR-34 | Follow-up Appointment | The Doctor creates a follow-up appointment for patients who need periodic monitoring. The follow-up date must be after the current visit date and is printed on a follow-up slip with a unique slip number. | UC-61, UC-62 |
| BR-35 | Medical Record Access | Doctors can view and export as PDF the medical records of all patients, including examination history and paraclinical results of all visits. Only an uncompleted visit can be edited; a closed record is locked (BR-32). | UC-51, UC-52, UC-53 |
| BR-36 | Receipt Handling | Receipts are generated automatically by the system; the Cashier cannot create them manually. Receipts are issued and printed by the Cashier at the counter. The software only records the Cashier’s “paid” confirmation; it does not process money transactions or accounting reconciliation. | UC-69, UC-70, UC-71, UC-72 |
| BR-37 | Payment Status & Receipt | A receipt has one of four statuses: Pending, Paid, Exempt, Cancelled; a receipt whose patient-payable amount is 0 automatically becomes Exempt. A printed receipt has a unique number, can only be printed after payment is confirmed, and lists each service with its insurance-covered amount and patient-paid amount. | UC-71, UC-72, UC-73 |
| BR-38 | Revenue Breakdown | Revenue statistics separate the insurance-covered amount from the patient-paid amount. | UC-31 |
| BR-39 | Examined Patient Report Scope | The examined patient list only shows patients examined by the logged-in Doctor in the selected period. This does not restrict medical record access (BR-35). | UC-34 |
| BR-40 | Room Reassignment | When an examination room cannot continue examining (for example, the doctor is unexpectedly absent), the Receptionist moves the room’s waiting patients to another active examination room, preferably of the same specialty, with a mandatory reason. Patients get the next queue numbers of the new room in the order they had in the old room, are marked “transferred” so they are called before regular patients (BR-18), and pay no additional examination fee. The system shows the new queue number and allows the examination ticket to be reprinted. | UC-40, UC-42 |
| BR-41 | Paraclinical Refusal | A patient refusing paraclinical services does not make the visit “Abandoned”. The Doctor cancels the refused services under the conditions in BR-25, with a mandatory reason; the receipt is recalculated. A visit with no remaining paraclinical services to perform moves to waiting for conclusion. | UC-49, UC-56, UC-69, UC-73 |
| BR-42 | Audit Trail | The system logs every view, creation, change, cancellation and export of medical record data with user, time and old/new values. Logs cannot be edited and are viewable by Admin. | UC-51, UC-52, UC-53 |
| BR-43 | Record Export | Doctors export medical records as PDF (Ministry of Health form). Admin exports records as XML/JSON (medical record data exchange standard). Every export records its purpose: data exchange, archiving, provision to the patient or to a competent authority. | UC-53 |
| BR-44 | Record Retention | Closed medical records are kept for at least 10 years; they cannot be disposed of before the retention deadline. |  |
| BR-45 | Simulated Integrations | Connections to external systems, such as the health insurance portal, are simulated and can later be replaced by the real service. | UC-74 |

## **3\. Other Requirements** {#3.-other-requirements}

### **3.1 Data Retention** {#3.1-data-retention}

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| OR-01 | Medical records are kept for at least 10 years in accordance with the Law on Medical Examination and Treatment. *(Retention periods for special cases to be confirmed – Q-14.)* |
| OR-02 | Invoices are kept for at least 10 years. |
| OR-03 | Audit log entries are kept for at least 12 months and cannot be edited or deleted by any user. |

 

### **3.2 Printed Forms** {#3.2-printed-forms}

| ID | Form | Main content |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| PF-01 | Examination ticket | Hospital name, registration code, queue number, department and location, doctor, patient code and name, year of birth, visit type, coverage rate, priority mark, patient amount of the exam fee, payment instruction, date/time. |
| PF-02 | Paraclinical order | Patient information, registration code, order code, list of ordered services with performing departments and locations, ordering Doctor, date. |
| PF-03 | Paraclinical result | Patient information, service, result values/images, conclusion, Technician, date. |
| PF-04 | Examination conclusion | Patient information, vital signs, findings, diagnosis (ICD-10), conclusion, Doctor, date. |
| PF-05 | Prescription | Patient information, diagnosis, drugs (name, dosage, quantity, usage), follow-up date (if any), Doctor, date. Format follows the Ministry of Health prescription regulation. |
| PF-06 | Invoice / receipt | Invoice number, patient information, visit type, coverage rate, service lines with unit price, insurance amount and patient amount, totals, payment method, Cashier, paid time. |

 

### **3.3 Out of Scope** {#3.3-out-of-scope}

The following are not part of this version (see Report 2, Out-of-scope): inpatient care, emergency care and surgery; selling or dispensing medication and drug/medical supply inventory; payment gateways, accounting and settlement with Social Security (the system only records the payment method); real-time connection to the national health insurance portal (simulated only); direct integration with laboratory and imaging equipment; SMS/phone reminders for follow-up appointments; staff shift scheduling, attendance and payroll; patient-facing channels (mobile app, online booking, kiosk); multi-facility management.

### **3.4 Open Issues** {#3.4-open-issues}

| ID | Issue | Impact |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Q-04 | Integration with the current paraclinical result software. | SW-04 |
| Q-09 / BR-14 | How the insurance rule "no repeated examination of the same content within one week if the previous result was normal" is checked. | BR-13, BR-27, UC-49 Order Paraclinical Services |
| Q-14 | Official Ministry of Health forms for electronic medical records. | OR-01, PF-\* |
| Q-15 | Whether doctor shift scheduling is added to the scope. | Scope |
| Q-18 | Handling a skipped patient who is still absent after the recall. | BR-21, BR-22 |
